Bildad Kaggia in Nairobi in 1949]]
'''Bildad Mwaganu Kaggia''' (1921 – 7 March 2005) was a Kenyan nationalist, activist, and politician. Kaggia was a member of the Mau Mau Central Committee. After independence he became a Member of Parliament. He established himself as a militant, fiery nationalist who wanted to serve the poor and landless people. Because of this he fell out irreconcilably with [[Jomo Kenyatta]].

"", sections=[Section(title='==Early life==', content=""

Kaggia was born in 1921, at [[Dagoretti]], now part of [[Nairobi]], where his father had moved from his home district of [[Murang'a
column8: Mūrang'a District]].<ref>Kaggia, 2012: 1.</ref>\nTwo years later his father moved back to Murang’a. Kaggia schooled at Santamor Estate and later at the Church Missionary Society School at [[Kahuhia
column10: ū]]<nowiki/>hia. Kaggia did very well at the exams and was selected for the famous [[Alliance High School (Kenya)
column11:
Alliance High School]]. Unfortunately, his father was not able to raise the school fee and Kaggia had to take up a clerical job at the District Commissioners' Office at Murang’a. When the [[Second World War]] broke out, Kaggia was moved to the military recruiting office. 
Despite hating war, Kaggia decided to join the army to seize the opportunity to travel to south-west Asia. When the [[War Office]] in [[London]] decided to create a unit in Britain to rehabilitate captured African soldiers, Kaggia applied and got the post of company quarter-sergeant, the first African to get this post.
Most of the work in the army was routine and boring. During the years in the army Kaggia engaged in many correspondence courses (journalism, trade unionism and political science) which later would serve him well during his political career. His experiences in the army made him aware of the evils from racial discrimination and colonialism. In his opinion the foreign religions in Kenya were a stepping stone to colonialism and his people had to be liberated from this as well.<ref>Rosberg, 1985 (1966): 192–193.</ref>

""), Section(title='==Kaggia’s religion (Dini ya Kaggia)==', content=""

Back in Kenya (1946) Kaggia denounced the church in the church. His objective was to create a purely African movement, divorced from European denominations and entirely independent of the European Church's doctrine. The new doctrine should include African customs and traditions. Kaggia had large followings in Central Province. This alarmed the church and their leaders asked the government for help. Subsequently, many times Kaggia and his followers were arrested and imprisoned for holding illegal meetings.<ref>Kaggia, 2012: 49–55. Kinatti, 2008: 90–91</ref> Nevertheless, Kaggia's doctrine spread and he had followers from all denominations and his religion was spreading into other provinces, ultimately even reaching Nyanza.<ref>Rosberg, 1985: 193.</ref> Kaggia was opposed to giving the movement a name, but, the people started calling it Andu a Kaggia (Kaggia's people). Later this became Dini ya Kaggia (Kaggia's religion).<ref>Rosberg, 1985: 193.</ref>

Kaggia saw that indeed his religion was liberating the minds of people. They were no longer humble, European-fearing people; now they had the courage to attack the mzungu government. Consequently, Kaggia decided to leave the religious work to others and shifted his attention from spiritual liberation to political liberation.<ref>Kaggia, 2012: 55.</ref>

""), Section(title='==The Young Radical==', content=""
[[File:Bildad Kagia. Nairobi. 1964.jpg
column13: Bildad Kaggia in Nairobi in 1964]]\nWhen Kenyatta was elected chairman of [[Kenya African Union
column14:
KAU]] in 1947 Kaggia joined KAU hoping that it would become more militant. However, at national level KAU was barely functioning<ref>Spencer, 1977: 225–6</ref> and Kaggia shifted his interest to the trade unions. He admired the fire and militancy of leaders like Kubai en Makhan Singh. Kaggia founded the Clerks and Commercial Workers Union and in 1948 he became its chairman. This union became a member of the general union, the Labour Trade Union of East Africa. In 1950 Kaggia became president of Labour Trade Union of East Africa.<ref>Kaggia, 2012: 56</ref> The trade unions had much support in Nairobi and they took over the KAU branch Nairobi in 1951. Kaggia was elected its general secretary.

Later the trade unions tried to take over the national leadership of KAU but this failed when the president of KAU, Jomo Kenyatta, changed the election procedure at the last moment. This almost resulted in a split of KAU, but the 'militants' decided to remain in KAU for the sake of unity.<ref>Kaggia, 2012: 59; Spencer, 1977: 265.</ref>

Kaggia started vernacular newspapers like Inoora ria Gikuyu and later Afrika Mpya to report KAU activities.  These and other vernacular newspapers were instrumental in spreading the message of the militant leaders who advocated for independence.

Kaggia was a leading member of the KAU Study Circle which assisted its members with drafting memoranda, resolutions and discussions papers. He was the President of the Anti Federation League. This league was set up to oppose the proposed Federation with Central Africa, which would strengthen the white settlers' political control of these territories. The Anti-Federation League succeeded in its objective as Kenya did not join the Federation when in 1953 the Central African Federation of three British colonies: [[Northern Rhodesia]] (now [[Zambia]]), [[Southern Rhodesia]] (now [[Zimbabwe]]) and [[Nyasaland]] (now [[Malawi]]) was founded.<ref>Kaggia, 2012: 68–69.</ref>

As a member of the African Advisory Council, Kaggia campaigned actively against the Nairobi municipal Council apartheid by-laws, which had created separate European, Asian and African areas in Nairobi. Kaggia considered it as one of his biggest achievements that these by-laws were repealed by the Municipal Council.<ref>Kaggia, 2012: 73.</ref>

Despairing of constitutional change, he joined [[Kenya Land and Freedom Army
column15:
Mau Mau]] and sat on its central Committee.<ref>He admits as much on p. 116 of Kaggia 1975.</ref> On 20 October 1952, he, along with the rest of the [[Kapenguria Six]], was arrested in Operation Jock Scott, and charged ''inter alia'' with managing Mau Mau, and being a senior member of it. He was convicted at trial, and imprisoned until September 1961. Thereafter, he was confined to his home district. On 17 November 1961, all restrictions were lifted.

""), Section(title='==Independence and after==', content=""

In the 1963 elections, he won [[Kandara Constituency]] seat on a [[Kenya African National Union
column16: KANU]] ticket, and so had the distinction of a seat in independent Kenya's first parliament. Kaggia also served as a minister in the Kenyatta cabinet; his denunciations of corruption marked him out as a member of KANU's radical tendency. When [[Kenyatta]] and [[Tom Mboya
column17: Mboya]] combined to purge the KANU left, he was one of their victims, with Kenyatta making the trip to Kandara to campaign against him. He joined [[Oginga Odinga
column19: KPU]], but eventually retired from active politics in 1974, after failing to recapture his seat.\n\nKaggia was the leading Kenyan leftist of the colonial period; probably the strategic planner on Mau Mau's central committee; notably anti-racist;<ref>Kaggia made common cause with Asian workers and [[Makhan Singh (Kenyan politician)
column20: trade-unionists]] at a time when this was difficult and unpopular; after [[History of Kenya#Independent Kenya
column21:
Uhuru]], he strove to secure recognition of Kenyan Asians' part in the struggle for independence. See Adenekan.</ref> and uncompromisingly committed to the poor.<ref>He lived in, and campaigned for the dwellers of, one of Nairobi's biggest slums. See Adenekan.</ref>

column1: '''Ukur Yatani Kanacho''' (born 12 March 1967) is a Kenyan politician and ambassador, and was appointed as [[List of finance ministers of Kenya
column2: Finance Cabinet Secretary]] on 14 January 2020.<ref name=""bloomberg"">{{cite news
column3: title=Kenya's New Treasury Chief Pledges to Tighten Purse Strings

column1: Yatani served as the First Governor of [[Marsabit County]] from 2013 to 2017, was the Permanent Representative to the [[United Nations]] in Vienna from 2009 to 2012,<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title=New Permanent Representative of the Republic of Kenya Presents Credentials
column7: access-date=6 February 2018}}</ref> and served as the Member of Parliament for [[North Horr Constituency]] in 2006.<ref>{{Cite news
column9: title=High stakes in contest for governor seat
column12: language=en-UK}}</ref> In 2019 he served as the Cabinet Secretary for Labour and Social Protection.<ref>[https://www.nation.co.ke/video/news/4146788-4307590-g0itgnz/index.html 9 cabinet secretaries sworn in at State House – Daily Nation<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> In 2020 he was named Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury.<ref>{{Cite web
column14: title=Yatani confirmed National Treasury CS as President Kenyatta realigns cabinet » Capital News

column1: Yatani was born in 1967 in [[Forole]] of North Horr sub-county to Yatani Kanacho, a prominent Gabra elder. In 1975, he started school in Maikona, and was then transferred to North Horr Primary school in 1978. Yatani sat for his Certificate of Primary Education (CPE) IN 1981 and emerged the top student in the then Marsabit District. He was given a scholarship by the Jomo Kenyatta Foundation and he joined Garbatulla High school. He later joined Kabarnet High school for his A-levels between 1986 and 1987.

Yatani received his Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Sociology from [[Egerton University]] in 1991. In 2005, he joined the [[University of York]] in the UK and studied a Master of Public Administration and Public Policy.<ref>{{Cite web

Yatani became a District Officer for the Government of Kenya. Yatani quickly rose through the ranks from District Officer Cadet to a Senior District Officer and then promoted to a District Commissioner in July 2002. In this position he successfully coordinated state business, managed government resources, maintained law and order, directed disaster relief operations, and implemented long term strategic plans that improved government services and the lives of local residents.<ref>{{Cite news
column2: title=Ukur Yattani Biography and Contacts - Softkenya.com

column1: Yatani was then called home by his constituents and elected as the Member of Parliament for North Horr constituency in 2006. During this time the Marsabit North District was created and M.P. Yatani spearheaded the formation of several administrative units across the constituency, leading to more independence and general improvement of service delivery.

Yatani was then appointed as the Assistant Minister, Ministry of Science and Technology. In this position he offered policy direction to the ministry, represented the government in local and international talks and negotiations, and assisted the Minister in performing of all ministerial and government functions.

In 2009, Yatani began a multi-year mission to advance the interests of Kenya on the international stage. He was named Ambassador to Austria in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Kenya's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Vienna.<ref>{{Cite news
column3: title=What Didn't Know About CS Ukur Yatani Appointed By Uhuru To Head Labour Docket
column7: language=en-US}}</ref> As the Ambassador to Austria, with accreditation to Hungary and Slovakia, he provided support and consular services to Kenyans living abroad and promoted trade and economic cooperation with a variety of European nations and thereby contributed to the realization of Kenya's Vision 2030. Amb. Yatani also served as the [[Board of Governors
column8: Board of Governors of the International Atomic Energy Agency]] for the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA), which works to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy around the world. Among the many accomplishments of the IAEA during Yatani's tenure, was the strategic use of strength and diplomacy to deescalate and safeguard Iran's nuclear capacity.<ref>{{Cite web

column1: In addition to this, Yatani held senior leadership positions at various diplomatic and international agencies at the United Nations and also chaired the African Group of Ambassadors.<ref>{{Cite news
column3: title=Marsabit County: Ukur Yattani Kanacho profile

column1: In the [[2013 Marsabit local elections]] Yatani was elected to pioneer the devolved County Government becoming the leader of the largest county in the nation. As the [[Marsabit County]] Governor he was tasked with building the newly formed county from scratch, and as the chief executive he brought peace, development and economic prosperity to the region.<ref>{{Citation

During his time as Governor, Yatani provided strategic leadership, guidance and oversight in setting up devolved governance structures, competent financial and human resource infrastructure and shaped the development agenda of Marsabit County. Throughout his term he promoted harmonious coexistence and cohesion among the fifteen indigenous ethnic communities and made Marsabit County one of the most peaceful in the country.<ref>{{Citation

Yatani set out on an ambitious development journey and steered the roll-out of the County Integrated Development Plan (hailed as the best in the country by the UN) which included a variety of major initiatives, including the construction of new county offices, a four-storey modern market, a modern stadium, over a dozen health centers, and new tourist resort facility and 200 ECD classrooms.<ref>{{Citation

The Yatani Government upgraded 5,000 kilometers of gravel roads, tarmacked Marsabit town roads, and drilling & operationalizing over fifty boreholes. During his tenure he established two referral hospitals, and purchased two dozen ambulances.<ref>{{Citation
column6: accessdate=6 February 2018}}</ref> He oversaw the installation of solar-based street lighting and drainage systems and stimulated an economic revival through investments in agriculture and livestock. Throughout his term he heavily supported cultural festivals<ref>{{Citation
column11: accessdate=6 February 2018}}</ref> and the Lake Turkana Cultural Festival was nominated for India's prestigious [[Tagore Award]].[[File:Ukur-Yatani-Kanacho-at-Lake-Turkana-Festival.jpg
column13: Ukur Yatani Kanacho dancing at the Lake Turkana Cultural Festival]]

column1: Yatani created strategic partnerships with the national government and major investors to bring two new roads to the county, as well as the largest wind power plant in Africa. In addition, he spearheaded a UNDP funded unique cross border program bringing jobs and billions of shillings of investment to the region. He also gained major external funding from the African Development Bank to create a livestock quarantine zone, modern abattoir and to develop international export markets for Marsabit's livestock products.<ref>{{Cite news
column3: title=Marsabit one-stop border point to start operations this month

column1: On 16 February 2018, Yatani was sworn in by the President of the Republic of Kenya, [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] for Cabinet Secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection.<ref>[https://www.nation.co.ke/video/news/4146788-4307590-g0itgnz/index.html 9 cabinet secretaries sworn in at State House – Daily Nation<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>
On 24 July 2019 President Uhuru Kenyatta appointed Yatani as the Cabinet Secretary for Treasury on Acting capacity following the sacking of Henry Rotich.<ref>{{Cite news
column3: title=Marsabit governor supports education by offering scholarship
column9: url-status=dead}}</ref> He was confirmed as the Cabinet Secretary on 24 January 2020.

column45: date=May 2026}}\n\'\'\'Ukur Yatani Kanacho\'\'\' (born 12 March 1967) is a Kenyan politician and ambassador, and was appointed as [[List of finance ministers of Kenya
column46: Finance Cabinet Secretary]] on 14 January 2020.<ref name=""bloomberg"">{{cite news
column47: title=Kenya\'s New Treasury Chief Pledges to Tighten Purse Strings
column56: url-status=live }}</ref>\n\nYatani served as the First Governor of [[Marsabit County]] from 2013 to 2017, was the Permanent Representative to the [[United Nations]] in Vienna from 2009 to 2012,<ref>{{Cite web
column58: title=New Permanent Representative of the Republic of Kenya Presents Credentials
column62: access-date=6 February 2018}}</ref> and served as the Member of Parliament for [[North Horr Constituency]] in 2006.<ref>{{Cite news
column64: title=High stakes in contest for governor seat
column67: language=en-UK}}</ref> In 2019 he served as the Cabinet Secretary for Labour and Social Protection.<ref>[https://www.nation.co.ke/video/news/4146788-4307590-g0itgnz/index.html 9 cabinet secretaries sworn in at State House – Daily Nation<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> In 2020 he was named Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury.<ref>{{Cite web

', sections=[Section(title='== Early life and education ==', content='
Yatani was born in 1967 in [[Forole]] of North Horr sub-county to Yatani Kanacho, a prominent Gabra elder. In 1975, he started school in Maikona, and was then transferred to North Horr Primary school in 1978. Yatani sat for his Certificate of Primary Education (CPE) IN 1981 and emerged the top student in the then Marsabit District. He was given a scholarship by the Jomo Kenyatta Foundation and he joined Garbatulla High school. He later joined Kabarnet High school for his A-levels between 1986 and 1987.

Yatani received his Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Sociology from [[Egerton University]] in 1991. In 2005, he joined the [[University of York]] in the UK and studied a Master of Public Administration and Public Policy.<ref>{{Cite web
column77:
bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

'), Section(title='== Political life ==', content=""
Yatani became a District Officer for the Government of Kenya. Yatani quickly rose through the ranks from District Officer Cadet to a Senior District Officer and then promoted to a District Commissioner in July 2002. In this position he successfully coordinated state business, managed government resources, maintained law and order, directed disaster relief operations, and implemented long term strategic plans that improved government services and the lives of local residents.<ref>{{Cite news
column78: title=Ukur Yattani Biography and Contacts - Softkenya.com
column81:
language=en-US}}</ref>

Yatani was then called home by his constituents and elected as the Member of Parliament for North Horr constituency in 2006. During this time the Marsabit North District was created and M.P. Yatani spearheaded the formation of several administrative units across the constituency, leading to more independence and general improvement of service delivery.

Yatani was then appointed as the Assistant Minister, Ministry of Science and Technology. In this position he offered policy direction to the ministry, represented the government in local and international talks and negotiations, and assisted the Minister in performing of all ministerial and government functions.

In 2009, Yatani began a multi-year mission to advance the interests of Kenya on the international stage. He was named Ambassador to Austria in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Kenya's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Vienna.<ref>{{Cite news
column83: title=What Didn't Know About CS Ukur Yatani Appointed By Uhuru To Head Labour Docket
column87: language=en-US}}</ref> As the Ambassador to Austria, with accreditation to Hungary and Slovakia, he provided support and consular services to Kenyans living abroad and promoted trade and economic cooperation with a variety of European nations and thereby contributed to the realization of Kenya's Vision 2030. Amb. Yatani also served as the [[Board of Governors
column88: Board of Governors of the International Atomic Energy Agency]] for the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA), which works to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy around the world. Among the many accomplishments of the IAEA during Yatani's tenure, was the strategic use of strength and diplomacy to deescalate and safeguard Iran's nuclear capacity.<ref>{{Cite web
column94: access-date=6 February 2018}}</ref>\n\nIn addition to this, Yatani held senior leadership positions at various diplomatic and international agencies at the United Nations and also chaired the African Group of Ambassadors.<ref>{{Cite news
column96: title=Marsabit County: Ukur Yattani Kanacho profile
column102: bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>\n\nIn the [[2013 Marsabit local elections]] Yatani was elected to pioneer the devolved County Government becoming the leader of the largest county in the nation. As the [[Marsabit County]] Governor he was tasked with building the newly formed county from scratch, and as the chief executive he brought peace, development and economic prosperity to the region.<ref>{{Citation
column107: accessdate=6 February 2018}}</ref>\n\nDuring his time as Governor, Yatani provided strategic leadership, guidance and oversight in setting up devolved governance structures, competent financial and human resource infrastructure and shaped the development agenda of Marsabit County. Throughout his term he promoted harmonious coexistence and cohesion among the fifteen indigenous ethnic communities and made Marsabit County one of the most peaceful in the country.<ref>{{Citation
column112: accessdate=6 February 2018}}</ref>\n\nYatani set out on an ambitious development journey and steered the roll-out of the County Integrated Development Plan (hailed as the best in the country by the UN) which included a variety of major initiatives, including the construction of new county offices, a four-storey modern market, a modern stadium, over a dozen health centers, and new tourist resort facility and 200 ECD classrooms.<ref>{{Citation
column117: accessdate=6 February 2018}}</ref>\n\nThe Yatani Government upgraded 5,000 kilometers of gravel roads, tarmacked Marsabit town roads, and drilling & operationalizing over fifty boreholes. During his tenure he established two referral hospitals, and purchased two dozen ambulances.<ref>{{Citation
column122: accessdate=6 February 2018}}</ref> He oversaw the installation of solar-based street lighting and drainage systems and stimulated an economic revival through investments in agriculture and livestock. Throughout his term he heavily supported cultural festivals<ref>{{Citation
column127: accessdate=6 February 2018}}</ref> and the Lake Turkana Cultural Festival was nominated for India's prestigious [[Tagore Award]].[[File:Ukur-Yatani-Kanacho-at-Lake-Turkana-Festival.jpg
column129: Ukur Yatani Kanacho dancing at the Lake Turkana Cultural Festival]]\n\nYatani created strategic partnerships with the national government and major investors to bring two new roads to the county, as well as the largest wind power plant in Africa. In addition, he spearheaded a UNDP funded unique cross border program bringing jobs and billions of shillings of investment to the region. He also gained major external funding from the African Development Bank to create a livestock quarantine zone, modern abattoir and to develop international export markets for Marsabit's livestock products.<ref>{{Cite news
column131: title=Marsabit one-stop border point to start operations this month
column136:
bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

On 16 February 2018, Yatani was sworn in by the President of the Republic of Kenya, [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] for Cabinet Secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection.<ref>[https://www.nation.co.ke/video/news/4146788-4307590-g0itgnz/index.html 9 cabinet secretaries sworn in at State House – Daily Nation<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

On 24 July 2019 President Uhuru Kenyatta appointed Yatani as the Cabinet Secretary for Treasury on Acting capacity following the sacking of Henry Rotich.<ref>{{Cite news
column138: title=Marsabit governor supports education by offering scholarship
column144:
url-status=dead}}</ref> He was confirmed as the Cabinet Secretary on 24 January 2020.

column1: '''Simeon Nyachae''' (6 February 1932 – 1 February 2021) was a Kenyan politician, government minister in both the [[Presidency of Daniel arap Moi
column2: Moi administration]] and [[Presidency of Mwai Kibaki
column3: the Kibaki administration]], as well as a businessman from [[Kisii County]].<ref name=""1R"">{{cite web
column5: title=This is how Simeon Nyachae made his wealth

column1: He invested in London, South Africa, Brazil, Zimbabwe, Australia and the US.{{Cn
Nyachae was born into a large [[Polygamy
column2: polygamous]] family in Nyaribari, in the then [[South Nyanza District
column3: South Kavirondo District]] of [[Nyanza Province]] in Kenya Colony, on 6 February 1932 to colonial chief Musa Nyandusi and the late Pauline Bosibori Nyandusi. In 1941, his father enrolled him in the Nyanchwa [[Seventh-day Adventist Church
column4: Seventh-day Adventist]] School, and in 1947, he joined the Kereri Intermediate School. Two years later, in 1949, he joined the Kisii Government African School but withdrew in 1953, just a year before he was due to sit for the Ordinary Level School Certificate. He then took up employment at his father's chief's camp as a district clerk.<ref name=""2R"">{{cite web
column11: location=Nairobi}}</ref> He later attended [[Torquay Academy]] and [[Churchill College, Cambridge]], both in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web
column13: title=The Life & Times of Simeon Nyachae

column1: Nyachae's career in the civil service began at this point. In 1957, he went to study public administration in London, returning to Kenya in 1960. Upon his return, Nyachae was posted as a district officer in [[Kangundo]] Division and later returned to [[Churchill College]], [[Cambridge]] for a diploma course in public administration. He became a district commissioner by December 1963.<ref name=""3R"">{{cite web
column7: title=The influential Young Turks of the 60s

column2: format=Archived from the original on 9 January 2004
column4: location=Nairobi}}</ref> Upon his arrival back in Kenya in 1964, he went back to provincial administration and began to steadily rise up the ranks within the provincial administration, ending up with a position as a provincial commissioner from 1965 to 1979. He later served as the chief secretary in the civil service under the governments of [[Jomo Kenyatta]] and [[Daniel Arap Moi]].<ref name=""3R""/>

column1: Upon his retirement from the civil service, Nyachae was arguably one of the most prominent personalities from Kisii County.<ref name=""1R""/> He won a parliamentary seat in 1992. His election in [[Nyaribari Chache Constituency]] was instrumental in his entry into the Moi government as a cabinet minister first for agriculture and later for finance.<ref name=""4R"">{{cite web
column2: format=Archived from the original on 27 May 2011
column9: title=Book Review: Walking Through The Corridor of Services – Hard Cover, by Simeon Nyachae

column1: In 1999, he fell out of favor with Moi and resigned from the government after having been moved to the less influential Ministry of Industry. He also left the [[Kenya African National Union]] (KANU) to join the opposition, [[Forum for the Restoration of Democracy-People
column2: Ford–People]], which was by then only a small party with roots in Central Kenya and three deputies in parliament.<ref name=""5R"">{{cite web
column3: title=Ford–People Party To Join Jubilee Amid Resistance

column1: Nyachae's plans to run for the [[President of Kenya

column1: '''Ochilo George Mbogo Ayacko''' (born 1968)<ref name=""Lifeline"">[https://www.nation.co.ke/news/politics/Senate-victory-grants-Ayacko-new-lifeline/1064-4798194-10h8h2n/index.html Senate victory gives Ochilo Ayacko new political lifeline], by Elisha Otieno, in the ''[[Daily Nation]]''; published October 9, 2018; retrieved March 27, 2020</ref> is a Kenyan politician who has served as the governor of [[Migori County]] since August 2022.<ref name=Swearing-In>[https://www.kbc.co.ke/dr-ochilo-ayacko-officially-assumes-office-of-migori-governor/ Dr Ochilo Ayacko officially assumes office of Migori Governor], by Beth Nyaga, at [[Kenya Broadcasting Corporation]]; published August 25, 2022; retrieved September 8, 2022</ref>

He previously represented [[Migori County]] in the [[Senate of Kenya]], beginning with the October 2018 by-election<ref name=""Clinches"">[https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2018-10-09-ochilo-ayacko-clinches-migori-senate-seat-with-85234-votes/ Ochilo Ayacko clinches Migori Senate seat with 85,234 votes], by Nancy Agutu, in ''[[The Star (Kenya)
column2: The Star]]''; published October 9, 2018; retrieved March 27, 2020</ref> to replace Senator [[Ben Oluoch]], who died in June 2018.<ref name=""Replace"">[https://citizentv.co.ke/news/ochillo-ayacko-leads-in-migori-senate-by-election-all-votes-in-214503 Ochillo Ayacko wins Migori Senate by-election], in CitizenTV.co.ke; published October 9, 2018; retrieved March 27, 2020</ref>

column1: '''Clement Michael George Argwings-Kodhek''' (26 October 1923 – 29 January 1969), also known as '''Chiedo Moa Gem Argwings-Kodhek''', was a Kenyan attorney and politician. He served in the government and cabinet of [[Jomo Kenyatta]], Kenya's first president, for six years, during which time he held the post of member of parliament for the [[Gem Constituency]] and the portfolios of Minister of Natural Resources and the [[Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs (Kenya)
A member of the Kagola Ojuodhi clan, Argwings-Kodhek was born in Nyawara, [[Nyanza Province]]. He was educated at [[St. Mary's School, Yala
column4: St. Mary's College]] in Kisubi, Uganda, where he sat for his [[University of Cambridge Local Examinations Syndicate
column5: Cambridge School Certificate]] in 1936. From 1937 until 1940 Argwings-Kodhek attended [[Makerere University
column6: Makerere College]], graduating from there with a teaching degree. After graduation, Argwings-Kodhek taught at [[Kapsabet High School
column7: Kapsabet Boys High School]] and in the Rift Valley.<ref>{{cite web
column8: title=Argwings-Kodhek: The politician history should never forget

column1: In 1947, Argwings-Kodhek won a scholarship from the Kenyan colonial government to study in [[Great Britain]]. Though sent to study the social sciences, Argwings-Kodhek's interests lay with the law, and he lost his scholarship when he switched to that subject, forcing his family to sell their assets in order to finance his education. After graduating from  [[Cardiff University
column2: University of South Wales]], Argwings-Kodhek was called to the bar at [[Lincoln’s Inn]], becoming the first East African to qualify as a barrister at the [[Inns of Court]] in London.<ref>{{cite web

column1: In 1952, Argwings-Kodhek returned to Kenya with his first wife, Mavis Tate. Though he was offered a position in the [[Attorney General of Kenya
column2: Department of the Attorney General]], he rejected the low salary — which was a third of that of his white peers — and went instead into private practice. A close associate of several members of the [[Kenya African Union]] (KAU), Argwings-Kodhek began taking briefs for KAU members charged with participating in the [[Mau Mau rebellion]]. Soon he was in such high demand among accused Mau Mau participants that Kenya's white settler population called him 'the Mau Mau lawyer'.<ref>{{cite book
column5: title=Histories of the Hanged: The Dirty War in Kenya and the End of Empire

column1: Many of the defendants who sought Argwings-Kodhek's services lacked the means to pay his fees. As a result, Argwings-Kodhek took their cases as '[[legal aid
column2: paupers' briefs]],' the low fees for which usually only covered his costs. His status as colonial Kenya's only Black lawyer exposed him to repeated harassment by police officers, who regularly requested his documentation and occasionally inhibited his access to areas affected by the state of emergency declared by the British.<ref>{{cite book
column5: title=Histories of the Hanged: The Dirty War in Kenya and the End of Empire
column10: page=156}}</ref> This harassment culminated with his [[disbarment]] in 1957.<ref>{{cite web
column13: title=Argwings Kodhek: A native upstart who dared marry a white woman

column1: Though national political parties were prohibited under the state of emergency proclaimed by the British, Argwings-Kodhek circumvented this ban in 1956 by establishing the [[Nairobi District African Congress]]. He was instrumental in the formation of the [[Kenya African National Union]] (KANU) in March 1960, and he won election to the colony's [[Legislative Council of Kenya
column2: Legislative Council]] in the [[1961 Kenyan general election
column3: 1961 general election]], serving on it until it replaced by the new [[Parliament of Kenya]] upon Kenya's independence in 1963.<ref>{{cite web
column4: title=First African lawyer to set up private practice in the country

column1: In the [[1963 Kenyan general election]], Argwings-Kodhek won election to the country's new [[House of Representatives (Kenya)
column2: House of Representatives]] as the representative for [[Gem Constituency]]. Appointed by Prime Minister [[Jomo Kenyatta]] as Assistant Minister for Defence, Argwings-Kodhek served in that office until he was promoted in 1966 to head the Ministry of Natural Resources. In 1968, he was named Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, serving in that office until his death in a [[traffic collision
column6: website=Official Website - Ministry of Foreign and Disapora Affairs

column2: Upper Hill]] at Ralph Bunche Road and runs west to the [[Valley Arcade]] area, is named after Argwings-Kodhek.<ref>{{Cite web

column2: Childs}}) and Ernest Albert Whitmee.<ref>{{Cite ODNB
column7: date=2023-05-11}}</ref> He spent much of his early life touring the country with his mother and attending various elementary schools until the age of twelve. column1: In 1928, he became chairman of the Shrewsbury [[Junior Imperial League]], and was elected to the local council as an independent conservative. His colonial career began in 1935 when he holidayed to [[Kenya]] and decided to move there (in 1936).

Vasey initially found work as a cinema manager, but soon got involved in local politics; being elected to Nairobi Municipal Council for the Westland's Ward in 1938. He later rose to [[Mayor of Nairobi]], serving between 1941-1942 and 1944-1946. Vasey married again in 1944 (it isn't clear what happened to his first wife). He was awarded a [[Companion of the Order of St Michael and St George]] (CMG) in 1945.

column1: '''Mvurya Salim Mgala''' (born 1970) is a Kenyan politician and Cabinet Secretary for Youth Affairs, Creative Economy and Sports of Kenya. He became the first governor of [[Kwale County]], Kenya after winning in the 2013 general elections. He vied on an Orange Democratic Movement ticket but later joined the [[Jubilee Party of Kenya]].<ref>{{cite web
column5: accessdate=15 February 2014}}</ref> It was announced on 30 August 2017 that he will be named Chairman of Kenya's Council of Governors. Unfortunately he didn't get to, instead governor Wycliffe Oparanya took over from NANOK. In October 2022, he was appointed the Cabinet Secretary for Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary.<ref>{{Cite web
column7: title='I'm worth Ksh. 120M', Mining CS nominee Salim Mvurya says

column1: Salim Mvurya was born at Kadzandani Village, Kinango District of [[Kwale County]]. He went to Mavirivirini Primary School in 1979 then Mpeketoni Secondary School from 1987 to 1990. He then proceeded to [[Egerton University]] for his first degree and graduated with Bachelors in Agri-Business Management in 1996. He holds a master's degree in Participation, Power and Social Change from the [[Institute of Development Studies]], in England, UK.<ref>{{cite web
column2: title=Former IDS student Salim Mvurya Mgala elected as County Governor in Kenyan elections
column4: publisher=Institute of Development Studies}}</ref> He also has further certificates in [[NGO]] management from MS-TCDC in [[Arusha]], Tanzania.

column1: Salim Mvurya has 17 years of social development and leadership experience. In the year 2008, he was appointed to be the Acting Country Director for [[Plan (aid organisation)
column2: Plan Kenya]]. Other organizations he has worked for include the [[Aga Khan Foundation]] and Tegemeo Institute of Agricultural Policy and Development (an institute of [[Egerton University]]). Some of the programs he implemented were funded by [[DFID]], [[USAID]], Ministries of Foreign Affairs in Netherlands and Finland, and [[NORAD]], Norway.

column1: In the 2013 general elections, Mvurya ran for Kwale governorship on an [[Orange Democratic Movement
column2: ODM]] ticket with [[Fatuma Achani]] as his running mate.<ref name=fatuma>{{Cite web
column3: title=The Governor – County Government of Kwale
column6: language=en-US}}</ref> His rivals were James Dena, Kassima Rigga Mambo, Simeon Mwero Mkalla and Mwarapayo Mohammed Mwachai. Mvurya won by more than half the votes cast.

column1: In May 2014, Mvurya ousted Nairobi governor [[Evans Kidero]] to become vice chairman of the Council of Governors.

On 29 September 2014 while at a rally with [[Raila Odinga]] in Kinango, Mvurya and Odinga were attacked by an elderly man who hit them on their backs with a stick. The security detail at the rally quickly subdued the man who was later released after it was established that he was mentally unstable.<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title = 'Mentally ill' man whips Raila at Coast rally}}</ref>

column1: After several months of speculation, Mvurya announced in September 2016 that he was leaving ODM and that he would run on a [[Jubilee Alliance]] ticket in the 2017 general elections.<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title = Jubilee wins big in Coast as Mvurya ditches ODM}}</ref> His deputy, Fatuma Achani, cited interference from other county chiefs in Kwale politics. Rumors claimed that senior officers in ODM had conspired to deny him the 2017 ODM ticket for his refusal to be loyal and working with Jubilee.{{citation needed
title = Governors to elect Salim Mvurya as chairman}}</ref> Kenya's Council of Governors agreed to elect Mvurya as the council's Chairman.<ref>{{Cite web
column5: title = Jubilee fronts Mvurya for Governors' Chair to smoothen inter-governmental relations » Capital News

column1: After two terms as governor, Mvurya was replaced in the next election when his deputy, Fatuma Achani, was elected governor in 2022.<ref name=fatuma/> She had been endorsed by Mvurya and their party and she was sworn in by Lady Justice [[Olga A. Sewe]].<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title=Kwale's Fatuma Achani makes history as she is sworn in first female Coast Governor

column1: '''Abon'go Malik''' ""'''Roy'''"" '''Obama''' (born March 17, 1958) is a Kenyan-American businessman and former political candidate known for being the paternal half-brother of former [[President of the United States]], [[Barack Obama]], and the eldest son of economist [[Barack Obama Sr.]]
Abon'go Malik ""Roy"" Obama was born and raised in [[Nairobi]], Kenya.<ref name=""slowlane"">{{Cite news
column5: title=Obama's Brother Chooses Life in Slow Lane
column14: title=Why Donald Trump is bringing Barack Obama's half-brother to the debate
column22: url-status=live }}</ref> His parents are economist [[Barack Obama Sr.]] and his first wife, [[Kezia Obama]] (née Nyandega).<ref>{{cite book
column25: title=The Other Barack: The Bold and Reckless Life of President Obama's Father
column33: access-date=26 July 2025}}</ref> Obama earned a degree in accounting from the [[University of Nairobi]].<ref>{{Cite book
column40: pages=265}}</ref> He met his younger half-brother, [[Barack Obama]], for the first time in 1985,<ref name=""slowlane"" /> when Barack flew from [[Chicago]] to [[Washington, D.C.]], to visit Malik.<ref>{{Cite book
column47: pages=262}}</ref> According to him, the two each served as [[best man]] at the other's wedding.<ref name=""slowlane"" /> Barack brought his wife, [[Michelle Obama]], to Kenya three years later, seeing Malik again while meeting many other relatives for the first time.<ref name=""sleepy"">{{Cite news
column51: title=Sleepy Little Village Where Obama Traces His Own Roots

column1: Malik Obama lives in the Obamas' ancestral home, [[Nyang'oma Kogelo]], a village of several hundred people, preferring its slow pace to that of the city.<ref name=slowlane/> Until 2004, he ran a small electronics shop a half-hour's drive away in another town.<ref name=slowlane/>  Since 2008, Obama has run the Barack H. Obama Foundation, founded in memory of his father, Barack Obama Sr.<ref>{{Cite web
column3: first=Andrea Suozzo, Ken Schwencke, Mike Tigas, Sisi Wei, Alec Glassford, Brandon
column5: title=Barack H Obama Foundation - Nonprofit Explorer
column13: title=Homepage - Welcome to The Barack H. Obama Foundation

column1: Obama is a dual citizen of both Kenya and the United States.<ref name="":1"">{{Cite web
column5: title=Who Is Malik Obama? At Last Debate, Trump Supporter And Half-Brother Of The President To Be Guest Of Republican Nominee
column11: url-status=live }}</ref> He is a frequent visitor to the United States,<ref name=""sleepy"" /> and works as a consultant in Washington, D.C., for several months each year.<ref name=slowlane/> He was registered to vote in [[Maryland]] as of 2016.<ref name="":0"" />

column1: During his half brother's [[Barack Obama 2008 presidential campaign
column2: 2008 presidential campaign]], Malik Obama was a spokesman for the extended Obama family in Kenya. He dealt with safety and privacy concerns arising from the increased attention from the press.<ref>{{Cite news
column6: title=We cannot lay claims on Obama; he's not one of us – Obama in this world
column12: url-status=live }}</ref> In early 2013, Obama ran for governor of the Kenyan county of [[Siaya County
column17: title=Obama's Step-Brother Will Seek Governorship of Kenyan County
column23: url-status=live }}</ref> His campaign slogan was ""Obama here, Obama there"" in reference to his half-brother who was serving his second term as the President of the United States. Obama garnered 2,792 votes, about 140,000 votes behind the eventual winner.<ref>{{Cite news
column27: title=President Obama's Brother Loses Election in Kenya

column1: Prior to the [[2016 United States presidential election]], Obama stated that he supported [[Donald Trump]], the candidate for the [[Republican Party (United States)
column6: title=Why Obama's half-brother says he'll be voting for Donald Trump
column12: url-status=live}}</ref> He attended the third presidential debate as one of Trump's guests.<ref>{{Cite magazine
column16: title=Donald Trump Is Bringing President Obama's Half-Brother to the Third Debate
column24: url-status=live}}</ref> On June 12, 2020, Malik Obama reportedly endorsed United States president Donald Trump,<ref>{{Cite web
column27: title=Malik Obama Throws Support Behind Donald Trump, William Ruto
column33: url-status=live}}</ref> and later in the week posted a fake and historically inaccurate birth certificate of Barack Obama in support of the [[Barack Obama citizenship conspiracy theories]]. The birth certificate alleges the US president was born in the Republic of Kenya in 1961, despite the [[Kenya
column34: Republic of Kenya]] not being founded until December 12, 1964.<ref>{{Cite web
column38: title=Obama's Brother Malik Tweets FAKE Birth Certificate Showing Obama Was Born in Kenya, Calls Him 'Stingy'
column48: title=Malik Obama Tweets Fake Barack Obama's Kenyan Birth Certificate
column54: website=www.mwakilishi.com}}</ref> The faux Kenyan certificate also contained a seal which read [[South Australia]],<ref>{{Cite web
column61: url-status=live }}</ref> further affirming its lack of authenticity. His sister [[Auma Obama
column62: Auma]] (among others) condemned him for promoting the theory.<ref>{{Cite web
column63: title=Auma Obama calls out brother Malik over fake Barack Obama birth certificate
column71: url-status=live}}</ref> Since then, he has consistently taken to news sites to express his adverse opinions about his brother, alleging that he made [[Deal with the Devil
column72: a pact with the Devil]].<ref>{{Cite web
column74: title='Sold His Soul to the Devil': Barack Obama's Estranged Brother Malik Shares Throwback Photo of the Former President, Calls Him a 'Snake' and a 'Trader' In Twitter Rant

column1: '''Joseph Jama Ole Lenku''' (born 20 October 1970) is a Kenyan politician who is the second Governor of [[Kajiado County]] after winning in the [[2017 Kenyan general election
column2: Kenyan General Elections]] on 8 August 2017 and retained his seat in the 2022 General elections held on 8 August. Lenku was Cabinet Secretary for Interior and Coordination of National Government from 2013 to 2014.

column1: Ole Lenku is a graduate of the [[University of Nairobi]], where he obtained his [[Master of Business Administration]] in strategic management and [[Bachelor of Commerce]] in Marketing. He has worked in different management positions for various hotels in Kenya and [[Tanzania]].
On 23 May 2013, Ole Lenku was appointed [[Cabinet Secretary]] in [[Uhuru Kenyatta
column2: President Uhuru Kenyatta's]] cabinet, surprisingly with no experience on security matters, becoming the only [[Maasai people
column3: Maasai]] person appointed and the pioneering chief executive of the newly created ministry under [[Constitution of Kenya
column7: title=President Uhuru Kenyatta nominates Kazungu Kambi, Joseph ole Lenku to Cabinet
column11: access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> During his first year in office, Ole Lenku steered significant reforms in the security sector, including a robust crack-down on drug trafficking, reforms of the police force and increase in its budget and devolution of security. In the wake of the terrorist attack on the [[Westgate mall attack
column12: Westgate Mall]] in September 2013, Lenku spearheaded the rolling out of a new security framework known as ""Nyumba Kumi"" (ten households) anchored on the larger concept of [[community policing]].<ref>{{cite web
column15: title=Kenya security to be enforced at the household

column1: Ole Lenku's appointment came as Kenya was transitioning to a new constitutional dispensation as well as a devolved government. His tenure as Cabinet Secretary has also been met with increased acts of terrorism culminating in the [[Westgate shopping mall attack
column2: Westgate Mall attack]], which left 69 dead and scores of people injured.<ref>{{cite news
column7: date=21 September 2013}}</ref> On 17 June 2014, Lenku dismissed calls for his resignation by the opposition and civil society led by the [[Law Society of Kenya]] (LSK).<ref>{{cite web
column10: title=LSK Calls for Lenku, Kimaiyo Resignation Over Killings
column14: access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> On 25 June 2014, Member of Parliament for Kisumu Central Ken Obura, a member of the [[Coalition for Reforms and Democracy]] (CORD) Now National Super Alliance (NASA), gave a notice of the motion to impeach Ole Lenku,<ref>{{cite web
column17: title=CORD PREPARES MOTION TO IMPEACH INTERIOR CS JOSEPH OLE LENKU

column1: Ole Lenku was born on 20 October 1970 in Lenkisim sub-location, Entonet location in the [[Loitokitok]] Division of [[Kajiado County]]. He spent his childhood like other Maasai boys in rural areas, herding goats and sheep, running errands and undergoing the necessary ceremonies, rituals and rites of passage in line with Maasai culture.<ref>{{cite web
column7: access-date=17 July 2014}}</ref> His father Lenku Ole Mpaa Kapei was a senior chief in Kajiado South. A respected leader of the Iterito age-group of the [[Maasai people
column8: Maasai]], he is reputedly one of the wealthiest Maasai leaders with more than 2,000 heads of cattle and a large family. His mother, Sentema Lenku, also hailed from the lineage of a powerful Maasai family. Keton ole Soipei, Lenku's maternal grandfather was second in line in the leadership of Iterito age-group having lost the top position to Kapei. On his father, Joseph Ole Lenku recalls that, ""Perhaps the only person who was wealthier than Ole Kapei in the region was Stanley Oloitiptip."" (The former Cabinet Minister and revered Maasai political kingpin who died on 22 January 1985). His double pedigree has placed Ole Lenku on the top rack of Maasai leadership, also widely viewed as the youthful leader in line to inherit the mantle of [[William Ole Ntimama]] as the community's spokesperson.<ref name=""Ole Lenku-Ole Ntimama"">{{cite web
column10: title=Is ole Lenku taking over from William ole Ntimama as Maasai spokesman?

column1: In 1979, Ole Lenku was enrolled to the Lenkisim Primary School. Because of the rough and tumble of [[Kajiado]], Ole Lenku had to be moved to three other elementary schools, including Ilbisel Primary School (1980–1981), Nkama Primary School (1982–1983) and D.E.B. Loitokitok (1984–1986), where he excelled in his [[Kenya Certificate of Primary Education
column2: Certificate of Primary Education]] (CPE) exams. In 1987, Ole Lenku proceeded to the [[Nakuru High School]], where he attained his [[Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education]] in 1990.<ref name="":0"">{{Cite web
column4: title=Joseph Ole Lenku: Reluctant warrior – Kenya Yearbook Editorial Board

column1: After high school, Ole Lenku was admitted to study at [[Kenyatta University]].  However, he proceeded to the Kenya Utalii College where he attained a diploma in Hotel Management in 1995.  He then proceeded to the [[University of Nairobi]] where he graduated in 2006 with a [[Bachelor of Commerce]] in Marketing and a [[Master of Business Administration]] in Business Administration. He further obtained a certificate in Project Management from [[Greece Ote Academy]] and a certificate in Corporate Governance (Centre for Corporate Governance), and has attended many other workshops and conferences on corporate governance, public service and security management.<ref name="":0"" />

Ole Lenku started his career in corporate sector management immediately after his graduation from the Kenya Utalii College. In 1996, he joined the prestigious [[Serena Hotels]], a chain of luxury resorts, safari lodges and hotels that operates in Eastern Africa ([[Kenya]], [[Tanzania]], [[Uganda]], [[Rwanda]] and [[Mozambique]]) and in Southern Asia ([[Afghanistan]], [[Pakistan]] and [[Tajikistan]]). He started off as Assistant Lodge Manager at Lake Manyara Serena Lodge in Tanzania where he served for two years.{{Citation needed

In 1998, Ole Lenku was moved to the Serengeti Serena, still in Tanzania. He developed training standards for the food and beverage departments for which he got commendation from the top leadership of Serena Hotels.<ref>{{cite web
column4: title=New additions to the Serena accolades
column11: url-status=dead}}</ref> He returned to Kenya in 1999, joining the Kilaguni Serena Lodge as a Lodge Manager. A year later, he was promoted to General Manager. He served in this corporate management position until 2003 when he joined the elective politics of [[Kajiado South Constituency

column1: In 2003, following the death of Kajiado South Member of Parliament Geoffrey Mepukori Parpai, Ole Lenku vied for the seat on the [[National Rainbow Coalition]] (NARC) ticket, but lost the nomination to [[Katoo Ole Metito]]. After the by-election, Ole Lenku resumed his corporate management career in the hospitality and tourism industry. In 2004, he was appointed General Manager of the David Livingstone Safari Resort, a five-star lodge in the [[Maasai Mara]] He served in this capacity until 2005 when he left the corporate sector and joined public service.{{Citation needed

In 2005, Ole Lenku joined government service, serving in the tourism and hospitality industry as the General Manager of Kenya Utali College, a state-owned corporation designed as the country's centre of excellence in technical training in the tourism and hospitality industry.<ref>{{cite web
column4: title=Farewell dinner for Cabinet Secretary Joseph Ole Lenku

column1: In 2006, Ole Lenku chaired a team that forged a partnership framework between the college and the [[Kenya Commercial Bank]] (KCB), enabling it to run the bank's [[Karen, Kenya
column2: Karen]] Leadership Centre. Moreover, between 2006 and 2009, Ole Lenku oversaw the execution of another partnership framework which enabled the Kenya Utalii College to manage the hospitality operations of the Kenya School of Monetary Studies. He served at the college until May 2013, when President Uhuru Kenyatta appointed him as the Cabinet Secretary for Interior and Coordination of National Government.<ref>{{Cite web

column1: President [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] appointed Ole Lenku as Cabinet Secretary for Interior and Coordination of National Government on 23 May 2013, becoming the third minister in the security docket to come from [[Kajiado County]], after [[George Saitoti]] and [[Katoo Ole Metito]].<ref>{{cite web
column3: title=News : Kazungu Kambi, Joseph Ole Lenku nominated to cabinet
column8: archive-date=28 July 2014 }}</ref> Like many of his predecessors in the security department, such as [[John Michuki]], Saitoti and Ole Metito, Ole Lenku did not have a background or training in security prior to his appointment. Critics, mainly in opposition, cited his training in hotel management and lack of prior background in security matters to demand for his sacking.<ref>{{cite web
column11: title=Sack Joseph ole Lenku, legislators tell President Uhuru Kenyatta

column1: Upon his appointment, Ole Lenku initiated police reforms focused on putting in place the relevant new structures and laws, dealing with the general resistance to reforms within the police service, speedy implementation of the new reforms, and dealing with the high corruptibility of police officers, inadequate management, supervision and monitoring of the force and lack of reasonable and transparent standards of vetting police recruits and those in service. The reforms have been internationally hailed as more successful than many thought. The [[Foreign Policy (magazine)
column2: Foreign Policy]] magazine noted that Kenya ""has actually made substantial—if incomplete and fragile—progress on police reform.""<ref>{{cite web
column5: title=Cleaning House in Kenya's Police Force
column9: access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref> Under Ole Lenku, the funding for police reforms increased remarkably from Kenya shilling 50 billion (approx. US$586 million) in 2012–13<ref>{{cite web
column12: title=Kenya prioritises security, education in new budget
column16: access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref> to Ksh. 67 billion (approx US$784 million) in the 2013–14 budget.<ref>{{cite web
column19: title=Kenyan budget allocates 67 billion shillings for police

column3: Westgate Mall]] in Nairobi, Ole Lenku spearheaded the Nyumba Kumi (ten households) security initiative aimed at bringing to the door step of individual citizens the mandate to ensure their own safety by knowing a few things about their neighbours as a security strategy to contain insecurity.<ref>{{cite web
column6: title=Nyumba Kumi initiative picks up in Kisumu
column10: access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref> On 7 October 2013, he announced that the government was working on a framework to put in place the Nyumba Kumi initiative across the country. He asked all County Commissioners to embark on its implementation to ensure security is enhanced in most parts of the country. In the same month, he unveiled a committee headed by a former provincial administrator, Joseph Kaguthi, to oversee the implementation of the Nyumba Kumi initiative that requires Kenyans to know at least ten households within their neighbourhood as a way of fighting crime.<ref>{{cite web
column13: title=Kaguthi to spearhead Nyumba Kumi initiative

column1: The initiative, modelled on the Tanzanian ""nyumba kumi"" structure, has reported success in formerly insecure areas like [[Kirinyaga District
column2: Kirinyaga East]] in central Kenya, but not in places like [[Lamu]] at the Coast where gangs have continued to terrorise communities.<ref>{{cite web
column12: archive-date=6 October 2014}}</ref> On 20 November 2013, Ole Lenku was forced to robustly defend the initiative from criticism by the opposition, which termed it unconstitutional.<ref>{{cite web
column15: title=Interior Secretary Ole Lenku says Nyumba Kumi will stay

column1: July 2013 alone saw high-profile deportation of 24 foreigners believed to be key members of drug cartels operating in Kenya and who had been in the past arrested on narcotic offences.<ref>{{cite web
column4: title=Kenya Kicks Out 24 Drug Traffickers in a Month
column11: fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Among those deported were Nigerians Anthony Chinedu and his brother Johnson Obina, whose deportation created a diplomatic crisis when the government of Nigeria held a Kenyan chartered plane, seven crew members and 12 security personnel at the [[Murtala Muhammed International Airport]] in [[Lagos]] for close to three weeks.<ref>{{cite web
column14: title=Nigeria-Kenya Standoff: Why Chinedu Must Return to Kenya
column21: archive-date=1 October 2015}}</ref> In another high-profile case, two South African women, Taran Louise Chukwu and Alicia Coetzer, were arrested and arraigned in court on charges of drug smuggling.<ref>{{cite web
column24: title=Another SA woman arrested in Kenya over drugs

column1: [[File:Governor Ole Lenku at his County Office.jpg

Joseph Ole Lenku assumed the office of the Governor on 8 August 2017. Since taking office he has implemented a series of reforms in the County Government and has focused development efforts in the sectors of Health, Lands and Education.

In the sector of health there are now 227 health facilities across the county and have seen significant improvements in almost all areas since 2017. The Kajiado Referral Hospital now a Level 5 facility complete with a renal unit with 500 patients have benefited from it saving them thousands of money and time they would have otherwise used in the private hospitals. There are 5 functional dialysis machines in the hospital. The new construction of a Maternal Child Health Complex with 2 theaters and wards with a bed capacity of 180 is about to open.{{Citation needed

One of the Governor's Flagship Projects is the Mbuzi Moja Afya Bora initiative which sensitizes the community to embrace health insurance as a means of reducing the out of pocket household expenditure. The department targeted 5,000 vulnerable households with an average membership of 5 people per household, bringing the total number of beneficiaries to 25,000 people. 3,512 households were realized during the exercise and this culminated in the auction which was presided over by H.E. the Deputy President where a total of KES 26 million was raised. All those who contributed a goat or paid KES 4,000 were registered and issued with an NHIF card and started benefiting from the insurance cover.{{Citation needed

Once a scourge in Kajiado County the lands sector has largely been turned around through a series of reforms and projects. These include the digitization of the land registry, a physical and digital validation of all plots in 28 towns, and the operationalizing a Geographic Information System Lab, the first county in Kenya to do so.{{Citation needed
In the Education sector many new ECE centres and classrooms were built, millions of shillings in bursaries distributed, and 67 new ECD teachers employed.{{Citation needed

Ole Lenku came under scrutiny as the Cabinet Secretary responsible for internal security after the [[Westgate Shopping Mall Attack]] where unidentified gunmen attacked the Westgate shopping mall in Nairobi on 21 September 2013. By 24 September, at least 67 people, including four attackers, were reported killed and 175 others wounded in the mass shooting. On 29 September, Kenya's Foreign Affairs Cabinet Secretary [[Amina Mohamed]] told the [[Public Broadcasting Service]] (PBS) that there was a woman involved in the attack. ""From the information that we have, two or three Americans (were involved) and I think, so far, I have heard of one Brit, a woman, and I think she has done this many times before.""<ref>{{cite web
column4: title=Americans and Briton 'among mall attackers', says Kenyan foreign minister
column9: access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref> This spurned speculation that the woman in question could be [[Samantha Lewthwaite]], also known as the ""White Widow"", who was wanted by Kenyan police over alleged links with a terrorist cell involved in attacks at the [[Coast Province (Kenya)
column10: Coast]]. Ole Lenku disputed the alleged presence of the British terrorist.<ref>{{cite news
column13: title=Tale of 'White Widow' Fills British Press

column1: Alleged reports of leaked intelligence files also surfaced in Kenyan papers, indicating that Kenya's top security agents knew of an ""increasing threat of terrorism"" days before the mall was attacked. The reports also alleged that the [[National Intelligence Service (Kenya)
column2: National Intelligence Service]] had issued warnings of a possible attack a year before. Ole Lenku declined to answer questions from journalists about possible intelligence failings, stating that intelligence issues were confidential and would not be discussed in public.<ref>{{cite news
column3: title=Kenyan minister evades questions on Westgate warnings
column7: access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref> The number of attackers involved in the attack was also a burning issue, oscillating between 4 and 15. Finally, Ole Lenku ascertained that four gunmen were involved in the killings, and reported that all of them were killed.<ref>{{cite web
column10: title=Kenya minister says 59 killed in mall attack

column1: After the siege, some quarters called for Ole Lenku's transfer to ""a lighter ministry"", but the Kenyatta government maintained that Lenku had the requisite management tools to run the ministry.<ref>{{cite web
column4: title=Ole Lenku has demonstrated that he is woefully inept

column1: Several Kenyans heavily criticised Ole Lenku after the crisis. On 5 April 2014, Bemih Kayonge of ''[[The Star (Kenya)
column2: The Star]]'' described him as ""gravely misinformed"" on matters of national security, adding that ever since it came into power, the Kenyatta government ""has shown no respect for the rule of law"".<ref>{{cite web
column4: title=On Tackling Insecurity, Ole Lenku Is Gravely Misinformed
column12: archive-date=17 May 2014 }}</ref> A writer at ''Bubblews'' called for Ole Lenku's resignation, stating that ""there has been increasing insecurity since he stepped into that office.""<ref>{{cite web

column1: Ole Lenku was back on the spotlight again after the [[2014 Mpeketoni attacks]], when marauding gunmen shot more than 60 people in and around [[Mpeketoni]] town in [[Lamu County]] between 15 and 17 June.<ref>{{cite news
column4: title=Kenya attack: Mpeketoni near Lamu hit by al-Shabab raid
column9: Al-Shabaab]] militant group claimed responsibility for the attacks, Ole Lenku said that the government was not ruling out a political link in the Mpeketoni attack.<ref>{{cite web
column12: title=Political link likely in Mpeketoni attack – Lenku
column17: access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref> A few days later, President [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] confirmed the political link stating that ""The attack was well planned, orchestrated and politically motivated ethnic violence against the Kenyan community with the intention of victimization for political reasons.""<ref>{{cite web
column20: title=Mpeketoni attack not work of Al Shabaab, says President Uhuru Kenyatta
column24: access-date=23 July 2014}}</ref> Over the next few days, Ole Lenku reiterated the President's message.

column1: [[Coalition for Reforms and Democracy]] (CORD) leader [[Raila Odinga]] called for Ole Lenku's resignation after the attacks, criticising the cabinet secretary over his statements that linked the attack to politics. The opposition, civil society, [[Senate of Kenya
column3: National Assembly]] representatives also called for Ole Lenku's resignation, citing his ministry's failure to adequately respond to the attacks.<ref>{{cite web
column5: title=Kenya: Cord Leader Raila Odinga Demands Lenku's Resignation

column1: Criticism against Ole Lenku reached fever pitch when on 22 November 2014 some 28 Kenyans travelling from the Northern town of Mandera were ordered off a bus and killed, with some of the bodies beheaded. Ten days later, on 2 December 2014, another 34 Kenyans who were asleep in a quarry in the outskirts of Mandera town were killed. Al Shabaab militiamen claimed responsibility for both attacks. Kenyans protested on the streets of Nairobi, calling for the removal of Ole Lenku and the Inspector General of Police, David Kimaiyo.{{Citation needed
The President succumbed to the pressure and announced that Ole Lenku had been dismissed, while the Inspector General of Police had resigned.{{Citation needed

After his unsuccessful debut into elective politics in 2003, Ole Lenku ventured into business and farming, and partly because of his cultural status as a leader in the Maasai community, he has kept a relatively large herd of cattle, estimated at 600 animals. He is married to Edna Chelangat Lenku, with whom he has four children.{{Citation needed

'''Joseph Jama Ole Lenku''' (born 20 October 1970) is a Kenyan politician who is the second Governor of [[Kajiado County]] after winning in the [[2017 Kenyan general election
column2: Kenyan General Elections]] on 8 August 2017 and retained his seat in the 2022 General elections held on 8 August. Lenku was Cabinet Secretary for Interior and Coordination of National Government from 2013 to 2014.

column1: Ole Lenku is a graduate of the [[University of Nairobi]], where he obtained his [[Master of Business Administration]] in strategic management and [[Bachelor of Commerce]] in Marketing. He has worked in different management positions for various hotels in Kenya and [[Tanzania]].
On 23 May 2013, Ole Lenku was appointed [[Cabinet Secretary]] in [[Uhuru Kenyatta
column2: President Uhuru Kenyatta's]] cabinet, surprisingly with no experience on security matters, becoming the only [[Maasai people
column3: Maasai]] person appointed and the pioneering chief executive of the newly created ministry under [[Constitution of Kenya
column7: title=President Uhuru Kenyatta nominates Kazungu Kambi, Joseph ole Lenku to Cabinet
column11: access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> During his first year in office, Ole Lenku steered significant reforms in the security sector, including a robust crack-down on drug trafficking, reforms of the police force and increase in its budget and devolution of security. In the wake of the terrorist attack on the [[Westgate mall attack
column12: Westgate Mall]] in September 2013, Lenku spearheaded the rolling out of a new security framework known as ""Nyumba Kumi"" (ten households) anchored on the larger concept of [[community policing]].<ref>{{cite web
column15: title=Kenya security to be enforced at the household

column1: Ole Lenku's appointment came as Kenya was transitioning to a new constitutional dispensation as well as a devolved government. His tenure as Cabinet Secretary has also been met with increased acts of terrorism culminating in the [[Westgate shopping mall attack
column2: Westgate Mall attack]], which left 69 dead and scores of people injured.<ref>{{cite news
column7: date=21 September 2013}}</ref> On 17 June 2014, Lenku dismissed calls for his resignation by the opposition and civil society led by the [[Law Society of Kenya]] (LSK).<ref>{{cite web
column10: title=LSK Calls for Lenku, Kimaiyo Resignation Over Killings
