', sections=[Section(title='==Early life and education==', content=""
Duale received his Certificate of Primary Education from Garissa Primary School in 1981. He then enrolled in Garissa High School where he received his [[Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education]] in 1985, and later joined [[Moi Forces Academy, Nairobi]] for his Kenya Advanced Certificate of Secondary Education, which he completed in 1987. He enrolled in [[Moi University]] for his undergraduate studies in education before transferring to [[Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology]] for his master's degree in business administration (MBA).<ref>{{Cite web
column121:
website=Parliament of Kenya}}</ref>

""), Section(title='==Early career==', content=""
In 1992, Duale began his teaching career as a graduate teacher at Sankuri Secondary School. He did, however, leave after two months and thereafter worked for six months as a clerical officer at the office of the provincial commissioner in Garissa.<ref>{{Cite web
column123: title=Aden Duale Profile: Education Background, Family & Career
column126: language=en-US}}</ref> After that, he worked for their family business until becoming a director for Kenya Broadcasting Cooperation from 1999 to 2003. He is the Livestock Marketing Society of Kenya's co-founder and CEO.<ref>{{Cite web
column130: title=Aden Duale Biography, Former Majority Leader National Assembly, Kenya
column134:
language=en-US}}</ref>

""), Section(title='==Political career==', content='
'), Section(title='===Member of the National Assembly===', content=""
Duale has served as a representative of the [[Dujis Constituency]] in the [[National Assembly of Kenya]] since the [[2007 Kenyan parliamentary election
column137: date=2008-06-16 }}. Parliament of Kenya. Accessed June 19, 2008.</ref> After initially being elected with the [[Orange Democratic Movement]], he switched parties for the [[2013 Kenya National Assembly elections
column138: 2013 elections]], and won re-election as a member of the [[United Republican Party (Kenya)
column139: United Republican Party]]. He also served as an assistant minister in the Ministry of Livestock Development between 2008 and 2013. In the 11th Parliament he was a member of the House Business and House Broadcasting Committees, while in the 12th Parliament he was a member of the House Business Committee.<ref>{{Cite web
column143: website=parliament.go.ke}}</ref>\n\nHe is known for sponsoring a bill which many consider 'a bill that killed student activism in Universities'. The bill introduced the electoral college system as opposed to the previous direct democracy system where university students directly elected their leaders. It required that students' associations would be constituted into electoral colleges based on their academic departments, schools, or faculties.<ref>{{Cite web
column144: title=How Aden Duale Bill killed student activism
column147: title=MPs Move to Change Students Leadership Law Fronted by Duale
column149:
work=Kenyans.co.ke}}</ref>
During his time as leader of the majority, Duale was the sponsor of an unsuccessful 2018 bill that would have reserved one in three seats in parliament for women.<ref>Nita Bhalla (28 November 2018), [https://www.reuters.com/article/kenya-women-politics-idAFL4N1Y34OD Kenyan MPs block drive for more women in politics]\xa0''[[Reuters]]''.</ref>

""), Section(title='== Cabinet position ==', content='
Duale was appointed defence cabinet secretary in Ruto's first cabinet in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web
column151: title=Ruto appoints Mudavadi, Duale, Ababu and others to cabinet
column155: language=en}}</ref> Early in his tenure as Cabinet Secretary for Defence, Duale officially deployed troops to eastern [[Democratic Republic of Congo]] to join an [[East African Community]] Joint Regional Force aiming to combat armed groups in the region.<ref name=""Kenya deploys troops to Congo to help end decades of bloodshed
column156:
Reuters"" />

On 23 May 2024, Duale was among the guests invited to the [[state dinner]] hosted by [[U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] in honor of President Ruto at the [[White House]].<ref>Minho Kim (23 May 2024), [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/23/us/politics/full-guest-list-biden-state-dinner-kenya.html The Full Guest List for Biden’s State Dinner With Kenya] ''[[New York Times]]''.</ref>

A cabinet reshuffle in July 2024 saw Duale removed from the defence docket and appointed to the Environment, Climate Change and Forestry docket.<ref>{{Cite web
column159: title=Surprise as Duale-Tuya swapped and Miano left out
column163: language=en}}</ref> He was later removed and on 25 March 2025, he took over the mantle to lead the [[Ministry of Health (Kenya)
column164: Ministry of Health]] as the Cabinet Secretary for Health from his predecessor [[Deborah Mlongo Barasa]] after another cabinet reshuffle.<ref>{{Cite web
column165: title=[Photos] Change of guard as CS Barasa hands over to Duale at MoH
column171: title=CS Duale commits to full implementation of Universal Health Coverage
column177: title=CS Muturi sacked, Duale becomes Health CS in Ruto Cabinet changes
column181: language=en}}</ref>\n\nHis tenure as Health CS has been riddled with scandals, the most recent one being the [[Social Health Authority Scandal]] where many ""ghost"" hospitals have claimed treatment payments worth billions of shillings with other existing hospitals falsifying patient records to receive money for services never offered to patients.<ref>{{Cite web
column187: work=Citizen Digital}}</ref> This has led to Kenyans and the opposition calling him out to resign for failing to address this with some accusing him of being complicit in the financial malfeasance. He has however maintained that he will not resign saying that his duty is to fix the country\'s health sector.<ref>{{Cite web
column188: title=Health CS Duale rejects calls to resign, says his duty is to fix health sector
column190: work=People Daily}}</ref> There have been threats for his impeachment from a section of lawmakers over the same.<ref>{{Cite web
column191: title=Kenya Moja lawmakers led by Edwin Sifuna threaten to impeach CS Duale over SHA fraud
column193: work=MSN }}</ref> He still maintains his stance and continues to serve the country under the docket.\n\nIn January 2026, new claims of fraudulent activities where Ksh.11 billion was lost within six months within the [[Social Health Authority (Kenya)
column194: Social Health Authority]] arose which he dismissed. He said, ""When I went there, that time I denied (it). After three weeks, I realized there was some truth about why Kenyans called it Mafia House, but today it is Afya House. Why should I resign? I don\'t need to resign. If I commit anything contrary to my oath of office, there are various ways of dealing with me: impeaching me by Parliament; the criminal justice system dealing with me if I have integrity issues; I\'m a political appointee, the President can one morning say I need another minister for Health,""<ref>{{Cite web
column196: title=\'I can\'t resign!\' Health CS Duale says amid alleged Ksh.11B loss at SHA
column200:
language=en-KE}}</ref>

column1: Dr. '''Mukhisa Kituyi''' (born October 20, 1956) is a Kenyan politician who served as Secretary-General of the [[United Nations Conference on Trade and Development]], [[UNCTAD]] from September 2013 to February 2021 when he stepped down to run for the Kenyan Presidency. Prior to joining UNCTAD, Kituyi was Chief Executive of the Kenya Institute of Governance, based in [[Nairobi]]. He served as Kenya's Minister of Trade and Industry from 2002 to 2007. He dropped his presidential bid in March 2022 to support former Prime Minister [[Raila Odinga]]. He began his education at Mbakalo DEB primary school.
He started his Primary Education at Mbakalo DEB Primary School in Mbakalo Ward. After attending [[St. Mary's School, Yala
column2: St. Mary's School]] in [[Yala, Kenya]],<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title= Curriculum Vitae Mukhisa Kituyi E.G.H., PhD
column4: url=https://www.brookings.edu/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/kituyim_cv.pdf}}</ref> Kituyi obtained a BA in Political Science and International Relations from [[Makerere University]] in [[Kampala]], [[Uganda]], graduating with honours and a PhD in Social Anthropology, a Master of Philosophy in Development Studies and a Diploma in Science, Comparative Production Systems, all from the [[University of Bergen]], [[Norway]].

column1: Prior to joining Parliament, Kituyi worked as director at the African Centre for Technology Studies (ACTS), Nairobi and as Programme Officer at the Norwegian Agency for International Development  [https://www.norad.no/en/front/ (NORAD)], also in Nairobi.

He was elected to the Kenyan Parliament in 1992, and was twice re-elected. He was Kenya's Minister of Trade and Industry from 2002 to 2007.  During this period, Kituyi chaired for two years the Council of Ministers of the [[Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa]] (COMESA) and the African Trade Ministers' Council.

He also served as chairman of the Council of Ministers of the African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) Group of States, and was lead negotiator for Eastern and Southern African ministers during the European Union-ACP Economic Partnership Agreement negotiations. He was convenor of the agriculture negotiations carried out at the World Trade Organization's Sixth Ministerial Conference held in Hong Kong, China in 2005.
From 2008 to 2012, Kituyi was a member of a team of experts advising the presidents of the nations of the [[East African Community]] on how to establish more effective regional economic links.
From 2011 to 2012, he was a consultant for the [[African Union Commission]], where he helped to develop the structure for a pan-African free trade area.

Immediately prior to becoming Secretary-General, Kituyi was Chief Executive of the Kenya Institute of Governance, based in Nairobi. The Institute is a think tank and advocacy organization that focuses on linking academic research and the development of public policy.
During 2012, Kituyi also served as a non-resident fellow of the Africa Growth Initiative of the [[Brookings Institution]], Washington, D.C. He was a resident scholar there in 2011.

He was first elected to Parliament on a [[Ford-Kenya]] ticket in 1992, becoming the Opposition [[Chief Whip]]. His predecessor was the late veteran politician, [[Elijah Mwangale]]. He was re-elected in 1997 and 2002. However, in the 2007 General Elections, he lost to newcomer [[Dr. David Simiyu Eseli
Kituyi left Ford-Kenya and joined [[Narc-Kenya]] and later [[New Ford Kenya]], a breakaway party formed by cabinet minister [[Soita Shitanda]].<ref>The Standard, November 21, 2007: {{usurped
column2: 1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20071122074221/http://www.eastandard.net/news/?id=1143977748 Ford-Kenya to oppose Kituyi, says Kombo]}}</ref>

column1: Kituyi is married to [[Dr. Ling Kituyi
column2: Ling Kituyi]] and they have four children. Ivar Makari Kituyi, Sitati Kituyi, Laila Kituyi and Thor Masaule Kituyi. On June 28, 2015, Ivar Makari Kituyi died at the age of 30. He suffered a diabetic attack. Ivar was buried at his father's Mbakalo Tongaren Constituency home.

column1: '''Wafula Wanyonyi Chebukati''' (19 December 1961 – 20 February 2025) was a Kenyan lawyer most known for serving as chairman of the [[Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission
column2: Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)]], which is responsible for overseeing elections in Kenya. Wafula Chebukati was appointed to the position on a six-year tenure in January 2017<ref>Capital FM, 18 January 2017 [https://www.capitalfm.co.ke/news/2017/01/president-kenyatta-appoints-chebukati-head-iebc/ President Kenyatta Appoints Chebukati To Head IEBC]</ref><ref>The Standard, 18 January 2017 [https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/counties/article/2000230400/uhuru-appoints-chebukati-as-new-iebc-chairman/ Uhuru Kenyatta appoints Chebukati as new IEBC Chairman]</ref> by the retired President of Kenya [[Uhuru Kenyatta]]. Following his appointment in 2017,<ref>Citizen Digital, 29 December 2016 [https://www.citizen.digital/news/uhuru-nominates-chebukati-as-iebc-chair-153373/ Uhuru Nominates Chebukati As IEBC Chair]</ref><ref>Nation, 30 December 2016 [https://nation.africa/kenya/news/politics/uhuru-nominates-wafula-chebukati-to-succeed-issack-hassan-as-iebc-boss-343192/ Uhuru nominates Wafula Chebukati to succeed Issack Hassan as IEBC boss]</ref> he succeeded<ref>Standard, 20 January 2017 [https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/counties/article/2000230672/issack-hassan-hands-over-office-to-new-iebc-chairperson-wafula-chebukati/ Issack Hassan hands over office to new IEBC Chairperson Wafula Chebukati]</ref><ref>The-Star, 20Jan 2017 [https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2017-01-20-time-up-issack-hassan-hands-over-to-new-iebc-boss-chebukati/ Time up: Issack Hassan hands over to new IEBC boss Chebukati]</ref> [[Ahmed Issack Hassan]]. He retired on 17 January 2023, following the end of his term.<ref name="":0"" /><ref name="":1"" /> He led Kenya through two heavily contested and controversial general elections; August 2017 and 2022 General Elections.

column1: His tenure at Kenya's electoral body was also one marred with resignation of IEBC commissioners, including his deputies, who faulted his leadership.<ref>{{Citation

Chebukati was a Kenyan lawyer with many years of experience. He ran his sole proprietorship law firm for 20 years and thereafter in 2006 he founded a Nairobi-based partnership law firm, [https://cootowlaw.com Cootow & Associates Advocates], which he resigned from on 17 January 2017, prior to taking up the job as a State Officer in accordance with the law and in order to avoid conflict of interest. In 2017, he was accused of conflict of interest by fronting his law firm for contracts at the IEBC but the matter was dismissed by Parliament for lack of evidence.<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title=Law firm linked to Chebukati got IEBC tenders for petitions
column10: title=Chebukati awarded his firm, fronted others for contracts, claims Chiloba
column14: language=en}}</ref> He was a politician and member of the [[Orange Democratic Movement]] party, which he resigned from before applying for the position of Chairperson of IEBC.<ref>Nation, 10 January 2017 [https://nation.africa/kenya/news/politics/i-resigned-from-odm-iebc-boss-nominee-wafula-chebukati-says-346638/ I resigned from ODM, IEBC boss-nominee Wafula Chebukati says]</ref> In 2007, he contested for the [[Saboti Constituency]] parliamentary seat and came in second place.<ref>{{Cite web
column17: title=I last met Raila in 2007, IEBC chairman nominee tells MPs

column1: In January 2017, he was appointed Chairperson of the [[Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission
column2: IEBC]].<ref>The-Star, 20 January 2017 [https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2017-01-20-chebukati-commissioners-sworn-in-to-head-iebc/ Chebukati, commissioners sworn in to head IEBC]</ref> During his tenure he managed three Kenyan elections: the [[2017 Kenyan general election]], [[October 2017 Kenyan presidential election]]<ref>Standard, 30 October 2017 [https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/article/2001258864/kenyans-react-after-chebukati-declares-uhuru-winner/ Kenyans react after Chebukati declares Uhuru winner]</ref><ref>KBC, 30 October 2017 [https://www.kbc.co.ke/iebc-set-declare-uhuru-kenyatta-president-elect/ IEBC Chair Chebukati declares Uhuru Kenyatta President-elect]</ref> and the [[2022 Kenyan general election]].<ref>The-Star, 16 August 2022 [https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2022-08-16-big-split-in-iebc-as-chebukati-declares-ruto-president-elect/ Big split in IEBC as Chebukati declares Ruto president-elect]</ref><ref>Capital FM, 2 September 2022 [https://www.capitalfm.co.ke/business/2022/09/chebukati-defends-executive-powers-in-declaring-ruto-president-elect/ Chebukati Defends Executive Powers In Declaring Ruto President-Elect]</ref>

column1: On 17 January 2023, Chebukati became the first Chairperson of the IEBC to successfully complete the 6-year constitutional term.<ref name="":0"">{{Cite web
column3: title=End of an era as Chebukati and two poll chiefs exit IEBC
column10: title=Which way IEBC? Chebukati, Guliye set to retire and commissioners wanted out
column14: language=en}}</ref> Chebukati was awarded Elder of the order of the Golden Heart (EGH) – Kenya's second highest award given to a civilian – by the President of Kenya.

column1: Seven months following his appointment at the IEBC, he oversaw the 2017 elections that saw the Supreme Court of Kenya historically nullify the presidential election results over electoral irregularities and illegalities.<ref>{{Cite news
column5: title=Kenya Supreme Court Nullifies Presidential Election
column10: issn=0362-4331}}</ref> During this period he had also lost two of his commissioners; Roslyn Akombe and his CEO Ezra Chiloba.<ref>{{Cite news
column12: title=Kenya election official Roselyn Akombe flees to US

column1: In 2018, IEBC Vice Chair Connie Nkatha Maina, together with fellow commissioners Margaret Mwachanya and Paul Kurgat, stood down from the electoral organising body citing the inability of the Commission's chairman Wafula Chebukati to lead IEBC effectively.<ref>{{Cite web
column2: title=Kenya electoral board commissioners resign over leadership fight

column1: During the 2022 presidential election, Chebukati found himself at the center of intense political controversy. As the head of the IEBC, he was responsible for overseeing the election that saw William Ruto declared the winner against Raila Odinga. However, the results were heavily contested, with Odinga and his supporters alleging electoral fraud and irregularities. The situation escalated when four out of the seven IEBC commissioners disowned the final results, citing lack of transparency in the tallying process.<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title=Four IEBC commissioners disown 2022 Presidential election results
column7: language=en-KE}}</ref> Chebukati, however, maintained that the election was conducted fairly and stood by the results,<ref>{{Cite web
column9: title=Chebukati resurfaces, insists 2022 polls results were the 'most credible'
column13: language=en}}</ref> a decision that led to threats, legal battles, and heightened political tensions in the country. The Supreme Court eventually upheld Ruto's victory, but the disputed election further divided public opinion on Chebukati's legacy as an election official.<ref>{{Cite web
column15: title=Supreme Court upholds William Ruto's Victory – Kenya News Agency

column1: Wafula Chebukati was born in Bungoma County on 22 December 1961. He was an alumnus of St Peters School Mumias, Bokoli Secondary school and Lenana School.<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title=High Schools Chebukati, Cherera and Other Ex-IEBC Commissioners Attended - Kenyans.co.ke

column1: '''Wafula Wanyonyi Chebukati''' (19 December 1961 – 20 February 2025) was a Kenyan lawyer most known for serving as chairman of the [[Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission
column2: Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)]], which is responsible for overseeing elections in Kenya. Wafula Chebukati was appointed to the position on a six-year tenure in January 2017<ref>Capital FM, 18 January 2017 [https://www.capitalfm.co.ke/news/2017/01/president-kenyatta-appoints-chebukati-head-iebc/ President Kenyatta Appoints Chebukati To Head IEBC]</ref><ref>The Standard, 18 January 2017 [https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/counties/article/2000230400/uhuru-appoints-chebukati-as-new-iebc-chairman/ Uhuru Kenyatta appoints Chebukati as new IEBC Chairman]</ref> by the retired President of Kenya [[Uhuru Kenyatta]]. Following his appointment in 2017,<ref>Citizen Digital, 29 December 2016 [https://www.citizen.digital/news/uhuru-nominates-chebukati-as-iebc-chair-153373/ Uhuru Nominates Chebukati As IEBC Chair]</ref><ref>Nation, 30 December 2016 [https://nation.africa/kenya/news/politics/uhuru-nominates-wafula-chebukati-to-succeed-issack-hassan-as-iebc-boss-343192/ Uhuru nominates Wafula Chebukati to succeed Issack Hassan as IEBC boss]</ref> he succeeded<ref>Standard, 20 January 2017 [https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/counties/article/2000230672/issack-hassan-hands-over-office-to-new-iebc-chairperson-wafula-chebukati/ Issack Hassan hands over office to new IEBC Chairperson Wafula Chebukati]</ref><ref>The-Star, 20Jan 2017 [https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2017-01-20-time-up-issack-hassan-hands-over-to-new-iebc-boss-chebukati/ Time up: Issack Hassan hands over to new IEBC boss Chebukati]</ref> [[Ahmed Issack Hassan]]. He retired on 17 January 2023, following the end of his term.<ref name="":0"" /><ref name="":1"" /> He led Kenya through two heavily contested and controversial general elections; August 2017 and 2022 General Elections.

column1: His tenure at Kenya's electoral body was also one marred with resignation of IEBC commissioners, including his deputies, who faulted his leadership.<ref>{{Citation

Chebukati was a Kenyan lawyer with many years of experience. He ran his sole proprietorship law firm for 20 years and thereafter in 2006 he founded a Nairobi-based partnership law firm, [https://cootowlaw.com Cootow & Associates Advocates], which he resigned from on 17 January 2017, prior to taking up the job as a State Officer in accordance with the law and in order to avoid conflict of interest. In 2017, he was accused of conflict of interest by fronting his law firm for contracts at the IEBC but the matter was dismissed by Parliament for lack of evidence.<ref>{{Cite web

column14: language=en}}</ref> He was a politician and member of the [[Orange Democratic Movement]] party, which he resigned from before applying for the position of Chairperson of IEBC.<ref>Nation, 10 January 2017 [https://nation.africa/kenya/news/politics/i-resigned-from-odm-iebc-boss-nominee-wafula-chebukati-says-346638/ I resigned from ODM, IEBC boss-nominee Wafula Chebukati says]</ref> In 2007, he contested for the [[Saboti Constituency]] parliamentary seat and came in second place.<ref>{{Cite web

column1: In 2018, IEBC Vice Chair Connie Nkatha Maina, together with fellow commissioners Margaret Mwachanya and Paul Kurgat, stood down from the electoral organising body citing the inability of the Commission's chairman Wafula Chebukati to lead IEBC effectively.<ref>{{Cite web
column2: title=Kenya electoral board commissioners resign over leadership fight

column1: During the 2022 presidential election, Chebukati found himself at the center of intense political controversy. As the head of the IEBC, he was responsible for overseeing the election that saw William Ruto declared the winner against Raila Odinga. However, the results were heavily contested, with Odinga and his supporters alleging electoral fraud and irregularities. The situation escalated when four out of the seven IEBC commissioners disowned the final results, citing lack of transparency in the tallying process.<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title=Four IEBC commissioners disown 2022 Presidential election results
column7: language=en-KE}}</ref> Chebukati, however, maintained that the election was conducted fairly and stood by the results,<ref>{{Cite web
column9: title=Chebukati resurfaces, insists 2022 polls results were the 'most credible'
column13: language=en}}</ref> a decision that led to threats, legal battles, and heightened political tensions in the country. The Supreme Court eventually upheld Ruto's victory, but the disputed election further divided public opinion on Chebukati's legacy as an election official.<ref>{{Cite web
column15: title=Supreme Court upholds William Ruto's Victory – Kenya News Agency

column1: '''Raphael Tuju''', [[Order of the Golden Heart of Kenya
column2: EGH]] (born 30 March 1959) is a Kenyan politician, media professional, and public servant. Before joining politics, he worked as a journalist, television producer, and communications consultant. He was the first African TV producer to win an International Emmy award for a documentary on health and development. In 2002, Tuju began his political career when he was elected as member of Parliament to represent Rarieda constituency, in Siaya County.

column1: Tuju attended Majiwa Primary School and Nakuru High School for his 4 years.  He then joined Starehe Boys Centre for 2 years for his senior o level.  He holds a Master of Arts (MA) degree in mass communications from the [[University of Leicester]], United Kingdom.<ref name=""ParliamentBio"">{{cite web
column7: website=Parliament of the Republic of Kenya
column9: title=Raphael Tuju Biography, Political Career, Wife, Awards

column1: Tuju worked as an anchor for television news in the late 1980s and early part of the 1990s on a part-time basis. He was a producer and director of several documentaries, radio and television commercials for international agencies, public sector institutions, and private-sector bodies. He was a columnist for local newspapers notably the ''[[The Standard (Kenya)

He worked as lead consultant in the design and implementation of several public communication programs for a varied clientele that included the [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) in Geneva, the [[World Bank]], the [[Department for International Development]] (DFID) of the British government, [[United States Agency for International Development]] (USAID), and the [[United Nations Development Programme]] (UNDP).<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" />
Between 1992 and 2001, he was a founder and director of Ace Communications.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" />
He has interests in the real estate sector.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" />

<blockquote>""In my younger years, I worked as a Television Producer with several documentary films to my credit and earning the distinction of being the first TV Producer in Africa to win an International Emmy award for a TV production. I mainly addressed health and human development issues in my communication career with HIV/AIDS and Gender Empowerment being the main subject matter and in which I am credited with some of the major groundbreaking marks in Kenya"".
In 2002, Tuju was elected as a member of parliament (MP) for [[Rarieda]] constituency in the [[2002 Kenyan general election
column2: December 2002 parliamentary election]]. He served until 2007 and managed to promote the education sector in the region by building new classrooms. He also implemented a major water project for the Rarieda people and introduced an innovative mobile hospital to reduce infant mortality as a result of malaria and HIV/AIDS.<ref name=""ParliamentBio"" /><ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" />

column1: The [[National Rainbow Coalition]] took power in 2003 and Tuju was appointed to the positions of Minister of Information and Communications and Minister for Tourism and Wildlife. He became more famous in 2005 for his feud with then the Roads and Infrastructure Minister [[Raila Odinga]]. His political career continued to shine despite many threats and was appointed to the [[List of Foreign Ministers of Kenya
column2: Foreign Minister]] docket on 8 December 2005 in a cabinet reshuffle.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" />

column1: He formed his Progressive People's Party (PPP) before the 2005 referendum with the aim of swaying votes away from the ""Orange No Campaign"" but defected his own party to join Narc-Kenya party through the LDP,  a move which his [[Rarieda Constituency
column2: Rarieda]] constituents and by extension the [[Luo people
column3: Luo]] Nyanza community treated as a betrayal to their loyalty.

column1: He also served as Kenya's Foreign Affairs Minister between 2005 and 2007.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" /> He is particularly remembered for his bravery when he sensibly warned the European governments during the 29th Asillah cultural festivals held in [[Morocco]] in 2007 for establishing policies which deprive African Development through trade partnership.<ref name=""StandardNdegwa20070806"">{{cite news
column4: title=Minister says Europe has bad trade policies
column13: access-date=23 May 2018}}</ref> He contested for Rarieda parliamentary seat in 2007 for the second time under the [[Party of National Unity (Kenya)
column14: Party of National Unity]] but was unsuccessful, he also lost his post as Minister for Foreign Affairs to [[Moses Wetangula]] under the former president Mwai Kibaki's government.<ref name=""StandardMurigi20080109"">{{cite news
column17: title=Kalonzo VP in Kibaki's new Cabinet

column1: He became the legal Advisor to the President of Kenya between 2008 and 2011 and he specialized on matters relating to media and the management of diversity. He was also a Special Envoy of the President on various missions.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" />
In 2012, Tuju launched his new political vehicle for the presidency, the Party of Action (POA) but did not go far with it. He later joined the former president [[Uhuru Kenyatta]]'s [[Jubilee Party
column2: Jubilee party]] and was elected as the party's Secretary General in 2017.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" /> He was later named by president as [[Minister without portfolio
column3: cabinet secretary without portfolio]] and served in this position until the end of their government's reign in 2022.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" /><ref name=""StarWasuna20180128"">{{cite news
column6: title=Uhuru nominates Tuju to be minister without docket

column1: Tuju was awarded the second highest civilian title in Kenya, E.G.H. (Elder of the [[Order of the Golden Heart of Kenya
column2: Golden Heart]]) by President [[Mwai Kibaki]] for his many years of service to the people of Kenya in the area of health, human development and public service.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" />

column1: In 1986, Tuju married [[Ruth Akinyi]]. They divorced in 2013. He has three children: two daughters and a son.<ref name=""SoftKenyaTujuBio"" /><ref name=""SDE2016"">{{cite web
column2: title=How Mrs Raphael Tuju fell from lavish Karen to grass

column1: On 12 February 2020, on the [[Nairobi–Nakuru–Mau Summit Highway
column2: Nairobi–Nakuru highway]], Tuju was involved in an auto accident while travelling to [[Kabarak]] to attend the burial of the late president of Kenya [[Daniel arap Moi]].<ref>{{cite news

EGH]] (born 30 March 1959) is a Kenyan politician, media professional, and public servant. Before joining politics, he worked as a journalist, television producer, and communications consultant. He was the first African TV producer to win an International Emmy award for a documentary on health and development. In 2002, Tuju began his political career when he was elected as member of Parliament to represent Rarieda constituency, in Siaya County.

Tuju worked as an anchor for television news in the late 1980s and early part of the 1990s on a part-time basis. He was a producer and director of several documentaries, radio and television commercials for international agencies, public sector institutions, and private-sector bodies. He was a columnist for local newspapers notably the ''[[The Standard (Kenya)
column37:
East African Standard]]''. He worked as lead consultant in the design and implementation of several public communication programs for a varied clientele that included the [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) in Geneva, the [[World Bank]], the [[Department for International Development]] (DFID) of the British government, [[United States Agency for International Development]] (USAID), and the [[United Nations Development Programme]] (UNDP). Between 1992 and 2001, he was a founder and director of Ace Communications. He has interests in the real estate sector. Of his accomplishments Tuju says,
""In my younger years, I worked as a Television Producer with several documentary films to my credit and earning the distinction of being the first TV Producer in Africa to win an International Emmy award for a TV production. I mainly addressed health and human development issues in my communication career with HIV/AIDS and Gender Empowerment being the main subject matter and in which I am credited with some of the major groundbreaking marks in Kenya"".

column40: Rarieda]] constituents and by extension the [[Luo people

column1: '''Mathias Benedict Keah''' (29 September 1943 – 25 July 2005) was a Kenyan politician and the Member of Parliament for [[Kaloleni Constituency]] in the Coast Province from 1988 to 2001.  During this period, he also served as an Assistant Minister in the Ministries of Finance, Land & Settlement and Transport & Communications respectively.

Keah was born on September 29, 1943, in [[Kizingo]] Village, [[Jibana]] Location in [[Kilifi District]].  He attended primary school in Kizingo after which joined St. Georges Secondary School for his Secondary Education. Thereafter, he joined [[Strathmore College]].<ref>{{cite web

He was an accountant by profession and was a member of the Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Kenya.  During his professional career, he worked at Accountancy & Audit firms and at a Parastatal after which he established his own Accountancy and Consultancy practice. Over the years, he sat in the  Boards of professional bodies and various international, regional and local financial and educational entities.
In 1987, Keah vied won the Kaloleni Parliamentary seat on a [[Kenya African National Union
column2: KANU]] ticket. He successfully retained the seat in the 1992 and 1997 elections before losing it to [[Morris Dzoro]] during the 2002 elections. During his political life, Keah also served as an Assistant Minister in the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Lands and Settlement and the Ministry of Transport and Communication.<ref>{{Cite web

column1: '''Eliud Wambu Mathu''' (1 June 1910 – 26 May 1993) was a Kenyan teacher, politician and civil servant. He was the first African member of the [[Legislative Council of Kenya]] and served from 1944 to 1957.<ref>{{Cite web
column2: title=Parliament of Kenya {{!}} The Kenyan Parliament Website

column1: Mathu was born on 1 June 1910, in [[Karai, Kenya]], to a [[Kikuyus
column2: Kikuyu]] family.<ref name=""auto1"">Andrew Burton, Andrew Ross Burton, Helene Charton-Bigot, Generations Past: Youth in East African History, Ohio University Press, 19 Oct 2010</ref> He was educated at the [[Alliance High School (Kenya)
column3: Alliance High School]] and qualified as a teacher. In 1929, he became the first African master at Alliance.<ref>{{cite journal
column4: title=Review: Understanding Kenya in the '50s: New Resources, but More Needed: Reviewed Works: Mathu of Kenya: A Political Study by Jack R. Roelker; Counter-Insurgency in Kenya 1952-60: A Study of Military Operations against Mau Mau by Anthony Clayton
column11: jstor=4185774}}</ref> Between 1932 and 1934, he studied at [[Fort Hare College]] in [[South Africa]] and passed the South Africa matriculation.<ref name=""auto1""/> He returned to teach at Alliance and pursued a Bachelor of Arts degree through a correspondence course.<ref name=""auto1""/> In 1938, he moved to the [[United Kingdom]] to complete a one-year teaching diploma from [[Exeter University]], and study history at [[Balliol College, Oxford]]. Mathu returned to Kenya in 1940, teaching at Alliance High School until he left in 1942 to open his own school in Waithaka.<ref name=""auto1""/>

column1: In October 1944, Mathu was nominated to the Legislative Council of Kenya to represent the African community. He became the first African member of the Council. He co-founded the [[Kenya African Union
column2: Kenya African Study Union]] to help co-ordinate and represent African interests in the Council. During the [[Mau Mau Uprising]] rival politicians from tribes deemed loyal to the government accused him of organising the Mau Mau. Despite remaining loyal himself, as a Kikuyu, he became disqualified from serving in the Council.<ref name=""auto2"">Munene, Macharia, Historical Reflections on Kenya: Intellectual Adventurism, Politics and International Relations, University of Nairobi Press, 16 Mar 2015</ref> At the [[1956–57 Kenyan general election
column3: 1957 election]], Mathu was replaced by [[Bernard Mate]], a member of the [[Meru people
column4: Meru tribe]] who had the support of the government.<ref name=""auto2""/>

column1: He died in [[Nairobi]] on 26 May 1993, aged 82.<ref>Kenya Gazette, 7 Oct 1994, Vol. 96, No. 48</ref>

column1: '''John Kìarie Wawerū''' (born 1978), commonly known as '''KJ''', is a Kenyan politician, comedian, media and communications professional, and educator. He has represented [[Dagoretti South Constituency]] in Nairobi County since 2017. Before entering politics, he was a co‑founder of the satirical comedy troupe Redykyulass and had a distinguished career across journalism, advertising, public campaigns, and board governance.<ref>{{Cite web

John Kìarie was born in [[Nairobi]] in 1978. He attended Kileleshwa Primary and [[Dagoretti High School]], excelling in drama, public speaking and science. He earned a BEd in Fine Art from [[Kenyatta University]] in 2001 and taught art and drama before returning to study at [[Daystar University]], where he received his MA in Development Communications in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web
column2: title=MP John Kiarie graduates with MA

column1: Hon. Kìarie began his professional journey at the [[Nation Media Group]] in 1995, serving as a correspondent and features cartoonist for the ''Sunday Nation'' and ''Daily Nation'' until 2007. His popular column, ""On a HEAD ON CORRISHON With the Youth,"" along with his in‐depth features, earned him a reputation for civic commentary.<ref name="":0"">{{Cite web
column6: quote=In 1994–2007: Features Cartoonist at Sunday Nation– Nation Media Group}}</ref>

column1: While still at Nation Media Group, Kìarie entered the advertising industry. In April 2008, he joined [[Ogilvy & Mather]] (later Ogilvy Kenya) as a junior creative, rising to Art Director. He then served as Associate Creative Director at [[McCann Erickson]] before moving on to become Creative Director at [[Scanad Group]] (2008–2011) and later as Creative Director, [[Ogilvy Africa]] (2008–2011). During this period, he worked on campaigns for clients such as [[Kenya Power]], [[Equity Bank Group]], EABL, PSK, GSK Kenya, and Coca-Cola, and was part of the pioneering teams that ""Africanised"" Kenyan advertising by integrating Sheng and other local languages into major campaigns.<ref>{{Cite web

From December 2008 to September 2012, Kìarie served as a Director on the [[Athi Water Services Board]], the regional water board overseeing 13 Water Services Companies (including Nairobi Water and Sewerage Company). He was elected Chairperson of the Strategy and Business Development Committee, guiding the board's planning and policy‐development initiatives.<ref name="":0"" /><ref>{{Cite web
column2: title=Board of Directors – Athi Water Works Development Agency

column1: Between 2003 and 2008, he also served as a Director at [[Youth Agenda]], where he helped design youth empowerment and civic‐education initiatives.<ref name="":0"" />

In October 2011, Kìarie co-founded Transcend Media Group, serving as Creative Director until November 2016. At Transcend, he led digital outreach and creative strategy for NGOs, public institutions (including the [[Communications Authority of Kenya]] and [[National Youth Service (Kenya)
column2: NYS]]), and corporate clients. Under his leadership, Transcend became known for youth-focused campaigns that combined strategic communication with civic engagement.<ref name="":0"" />

column1: In 1998, while at [[Kenyatta University]], Kìarie co-founded Redykyulass with Walter Mong'are and Tony Njuguna, renowned for political impersonations and satirical commentary targeting leaders like Moi and Kibaki.<ref>{{Cite news
column2: title=The funny side of Kenyan politics

column1: Redykyulass shaped Kenya's comedy scene—*The Standard* described them as ""Kenya's most influential comedy act.""<ref>{{Cite web

column1: '''John Kìarie Wawerū''' (born 1978), commonly known as '''KJ''', is a Kenyan politician, comedian, media and communications professional, and educator. He has represented [[Dagoretti South Constituency]] in Nairobi County since 2017. Before entering politics, he was a co‑founder of the satirical comedy troupe Redykyulass and had a distinguished career across journalism, advertising, public campaigns, and board governance.<ref>{{Cite web

John Kìarie was born in [[Nairobi]] in 1978. He attended Kileleshwa Primary and [[Dagoretti High School]], excelling in drama, public speaking and science. He earned a BEd in Fine Art from [[Kenyatta University]] in 2001 and taught art and drama before returning to study at [[Daystar University]], where he received his MA in Development Communications in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web
column2: title=MP John Kiarie graduates with MA

column1: Hon. Kìarie began his professional journey at the [[Nation Media Group]] in 1995, serving as a correspondent and features cartoonist for the ''Sunday Nation'' and ''Daily Nation'' until 2007. His popular column, ""On a HEAD ON CORRISHON With the Youth,"" along with his in‐depth features, earned him a reputation for civic commentary.<ref name="":0"">{{Cite web
column6: quote=In 1994–2007: Features Cartoonist at Sunday Nation– Nation Media Group}}</ref>

column1: While still at Nation Media Group, Kìarie entered the advertising industry. In April 2008, he joined [[Ogilvy & Mather]] (later Ogilvy Kenya) as a junior creative, rising to Art Director. He then served as Associate Creative Director at [[McCann Erickson]] before moving on to become Creative Director at [[Scanad Group]] (2008–2011) and later as Creative Director, [[Ogilvy Africa]] (2008–2011). During this period, he worked on campaigns for clients such as [[Kenya Power]], [[Equity Bank Group]], EABL, PSK, GSK Kenya, and Coca-Cola, and was part of the pioneering teams that ""Africanised"" Kenyan advertising by integrating Sheng and other local languages into major campaigns.<ref>{{Cite web

From December 2008 to September 2012, Kìarie served as a Director on the [[Athi Water Services Board]], the regional water board overseeing 13 Water Services Companies (including Nairobi Water and Sewerage Company). He was elected Chairperson of the Strategy and Business Development Committee, guiding the board's planning and policy‐development initiatives.<ref name="":0"" /><ref>{{Cite web
column2: title=Board of Directors – Athi Water Works Development Agency

column1: Between 2003 and 2008, he also served as a Director at [[Youth Agenda]], where he helped design youth empowerment and civic‐education initiatives.<ref name="":0"" />

In October 2011, Kìarie co-founded Transcend Media Group, serving as Creative Director until November 2016. At Transcend, he led digital outreach and creative strategy for NGOs, public institutions (including the [[Communications Authority of Kenya]] and [[National Youth Service (Kenya)
column2: NYS]]), and corporate clients. Under his leadership, Transcend became known for youth-focused campaigns that combined strategic communication with civic engagement.<ref name="":0"" />

column1: In 1998, while at [[Kenyatta University]], Kìarie co-founded Redykyulass with Walter Mong'are and Tony Njuguna, renowned for political impersonations and satirical commentary targeting leaders like Moi and Kibaki.<ref>{{Cite news

column1: '''G. G. Njuguna Ngengi''' (died January 2, 2008) was a Kenyan politician native to [[Molo, Kenya

He came into international attention in 1993 when he and an assistant, Mr. [[Koigi wa Wamwere]], were charged with violent robbery after they allegedly stormed the Bahati Police Station.<ref name=stan>''The Standard'', January 3, 2008: {{usurped
column2: 1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20080107051405/http://eastandard.net/news/?id=1143979848&cid=159 Politician killed in ethnic clashes]}}</ref> They were sentenced to prison following a controversial trial in 1995, a move that was condemned by the European Union <ref>Texts Adopted by European Parliament. Final Edition: 21 September 1995:  [http://www.europarl.europa.eu/pv2/pv2?PRG=CALDOC&TPV=DEF&FILE=950921&TXTLST=1&POS=1&LASTCHAP=9&SDOCTA=9&Type_Doc=FIRST&LANGUE=EN Resolution on unfair trials in Kenya]</ref> and Amnesty International <ref>Amnesty International [http://www.mirrorimage.com/ai/about/inspiration/wamwere.html KENYA: FORMER POC THANKS AIUSA ACTIVISTS AND STAFF] {{Webarchive
column4: date=2008-05-13 }}</ref> among others. Ngengi was released in 1997.<ref>Amnesty International: 1998 Annual Report on Kenya</ref>

column1: Ngengi was a councillor in Molo before his sentence.<ref name=""censor"">Global Campaign for Free Expression, March 1995: [http://www.article19.org/pdfs/publications/kenya-censorship-in-kenya.pdf CENSORSHIP IN KENYA - GOVERNMENT CRITICS FACE THE DEATH SENTENCE] {{Webarchive
column3: date=2008-10-11 }}</ref> He is also a former army captain.<ref>Daily Nation, June 3, 2002: [http://www.nationaudio.com/elections/constituencyreviews/Constituencies_Molo5.html Where soothing ethnic strife is the major task]</ref>

column1: His sister Josephine Nyawira Ngengi was arrested and charged in 1994 for allegedly robbing a supermarket.<ref name=""censor""/>

Ngengi was killed on January 2, 2008,  in [[Kuresoi]] during a meeting he was addressing in a bid to broker peace between the warring local communities following the controversial [[2007 Kenyan presidential election]].<ref name=stan/> Several armed youth came in and shot Ngengi with a bow before they hacked him to death.<ref name=stan/> According to Litabalia Achesa security was increased in the area following his death.<ref name=stan/>

column1: '''Quincy Zuma Wambitta Timberlake''' (born 22 April 1980) is a Kenyan political activist, occultist, and former presidential candidate, now resident in [[Australia]].<ref name=""trouble""/> Along with [[Esther Arunga]] and [[Joseph Hellon]], he is the co-founder of the PlaCenta Party (Platinum Centraliser and Unionist Party) of Kenya, which according to its manifesto aims ""to promote and protect individual rights and freedoms set forth in the Kenyan Constitution and to limit the scope of national government authority and spending.""<ref>[http://www.placentapartyofkenya.net/ ""Placenta Party of Kenya""] {{Webarchive
column3: date=24 December 2013 }} Retrieved on 20 October 2013.</ref><ref>Mango, Carole. [http://www.the-star.co.ke/news/article-85514/hellon-arunga-tell-coast-youth-reject-draft ""Hellon Arunga tell Coast youth to reject draft""] {{webarchive

column1: Timberlake came into the public eye after announcing his political ambitions in 2010<ref>[http://kenyadecides.co.ke/mp/quincy-timberlake/ ""Kenya Decides, Quincy Timberlake""] {{webarchive
column3: date=24 December 2013 }} Retrieved on 6 October 2013.</ref> and declaring that he would run for the [[Langata Constituency]] before the promulgation of the constitution. He later announced that he would contest the 2017 presidential election.<ref>Arlington, Darling. [http://www.allvoices.com/contributed-news/15781677-placenta-party-of-kenya-to-contest-2017-presidential-elections ""PlaCenta Party of Kenya to contest 2017 Presidential elections""] {{Webarchive

column1: The PlaCenta Party of Kenya was founded by Hellon, Timberlake and Arunga while they were still members of Hellon's Finger of God church.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KSEHtaYPm98, ""The Finger of God Trio Plans""]. [[Citizen TV]], 18 March 2010, Retrieved on 18 October 2013.</ref> Hellon later broke ties with the couple, claiming they had attempted to defraud him.<ref name=""trouble"">Kerongo, Grace. [http://www.the-star.co.ke/news/article-75228/finger-god-trouble-paradise ""Finger of God: Trouble in Paradise""] {{webarchive
column3: date=8 August 2014 }}, ''The Star'', 14 January 2011.</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WavFK2acyDw ""Joseph Helon Explains what happened to Esther Arunga""], KTN Kenya, 3 June 2014</ref>

column1: According to the party website, Project Take Back Kenya is an effort to break the rotational pattern of parties replacing names but featuring the same politicians at every election. The party's stated objective is to ""thrash the elite stranglehold on liberty, uniting Kenya's culturally diverse patriots who embrace traditional family values and restoring freedom of worship and expression.""<ref>[http://www.placentapartyofkenya.net/ ""Message from the President""] {{Webarchive
column3: date=24 December 2013 }}, Platinum Centraliser and Unionist Party. Retrieved on 20 October 2013.</ref>

column1: In 2010, Timberlake announced his intention to run for Prime Minister in the 2012 elections. A new Constitution was passed in the same year, bringing major amendments to the governing structure of the country.<ref>[https://www.voanews.com/a/kenyas-new-constitution-signed-into-law--101632883/124592.html ""Landmark moment as new Kenyan Constitution takes effect""], [[Voice of America]]. 26 August 2010.</ref> Timberlake then shifted his goal to contesting for the presidency. A number of court charges followed, which would have hindered him from contesting according to the law. Timberlake abandoned his presidential ambition and contested the seat of Lang'ata, the former PM's constituency.<ref>Kenya Decides. [http://kenyadecides.co.ke/mp/quincy-timberlake/ ""Quincy Timberlake for Lang'ata Constituency MP 2013""] {{webarchive
column3: date=24 December 2013 }}, [[Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission

column4: Timberlake arriving from [[Nyayo House]] under tight security to face charges of being a member of a cult before Chief Magistrate Gilbert Mutembei]]

column1: In February 2010, Hellon, Timberlake and Arunga announced their entry into politics under the umbrella of the PlaCenta Party of Kenya, with Hellon contesting for the presidency and Arunga for the seat of [[Karachuonyo Constituency]] and as a contender for the seat of Deputy President.<ref>Kenya Decides 2013. [http://kenyadecides.co.ke/mp/esther-timberlake/ ""Esther Timberlake for Karachuonyo Constituency MP 2013""] {{webarchive
column3: date=18 December 2014 }}, [[Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission
column4: IEBC]], 1 October 2012. Retrieved on 16 October 2013.</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KSEHtaYPm98 ""The Finger of God Trio Plans""], Citizen TV, 18 March 2010, Retrieved on 18 October 2013.</ref> On the same day that they made the announcement, Arunga resigned from her job as a news anchor at [[Kenya Television Network]]. Within hours of the announcement, Arunga and Hellon were arrested for being members of an illegal society, the Finger of God, an evangelical church which Mrs Timberlake had attended for a year. The church had been registered as legal by the government 5 years previously. Computers and laptops were destroyed, documents confiscated and vehicles impounded.<ref>[http://www.nation.co.ke/news/-/1056/866110/-/3ajj6xz/-/index.html ""Police arrest Arunga, Hellon""] ''The Daily Nation'', 21 February 2010</ref><ref>Momanyi, Bernard. [http://www.capitalfm.co.ke/lifestyle/2010/02/22/esther-arunga-and-joseph-hellon-arrested/ ""Esther Arunga and Joseph Hellon arrested""]. [[98.4 Capital FM
column5: Capital FM]], 22 February 2010.</ref> Timberlake was also arrested; while the rest of the group was released on bail after 2 days, he and Arunga were held in police custody. They both claim to have been isolated and tortured.<ref>''[[Kenyan Daily Post]]'', {{usurped
column6: [https://web.archive.org/web/20141108045420/http://www.jambonewspot.com/how-raila-ordered-esther-arungas-forceful-abortion/ ""How Raila ordered Esther Arunga's forceful abortion""]}}, Jambo News Spot, 14 July 2012, Retrieved on 21 October 2013.</ref> Timberlake spent months behind bars but was finally released with no charges in May 2011. Arunga, who had previously broken off her engagement to another church member, married him on 3 March while he was still in custody.<ref name=weds>[http://www.capitalfm.co.ke/lifestyle/2010/03/04/esther-arunga-weds-quincy-timberlake/ ""Esther Arunga weds Quincy Timberlake""], Capital FM, 4 March 2010.</ref>

column1: After being released from custody, Timberlake remained under house arrest for several months on suspicion of being in the country illegally<ref>Ombati, Cyrus. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?id=2000006846&cid=159&story=Timberlake%20held%20in%20probe%20into%20his%20nationality&articleID=2000006846, ""Timberlake held in probe into his nationality""], Nairobi, 2 April 2010, Retrieved on 16 October 2013.</ref> and planning a revolt against the government.<ref>Thuku, Wahome. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?id=%202000008648&cid=418&articleID=2000008648, ""Quincy Timberlake charged for passport forgery""], ''[[The Standard (Kenya)
column2: The Standard]]'', 28 April 2010.</ref><ref name=""Khalwale"">Ochami, David. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?id=%202000005386&cid=37&articleID=2000005386 ""Khalwale wants troublesome foreigners kicked out""], ''The Standard'', 11 March 2010.</ref> The arrests were widely publicised.<ref>Okungu, Jerry. [http://www.afroarticles.com/article-dashboard/Article/Esther-Arunga--TV-Personality-Dominates-Kenyan-Media-For-One-Whole-Week/201752, ""Esther Arunga; TV Personality Dominates Kenyan Media for One Whole Week""], AfroArticles, 24 February 2010, Retrieved on 16 October 2013.</ref>

column1: The couple was presented before the court on charges including being members of an illegal society (the Finger of God) and illegally holding passports from various countries.<ref name=""standardmedia.co.ke"">Kwamboka, Evelyn, [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?articleID=2000005378&story_title=Arunga-charged-with-being-member-of-unlawful-sect, ""Arunga Charged With Being a Member of an Unlawful Sect.""], ''The Standard'', 11 March 2010.</ref> The cases were postponed for several months. '''Quincy Zuma Wambitta Timberlake''' (born 22 April 1980) is a Kenyan political activist, occultist, and former presidential candidate, now resident in [[Australia]].<ref name=""trouble""/> Along with [[Esther Arunga]] and [[Joseph Hellon]], he is the co-founder of the PlaCenta Party (Platinum Centraliser and Unionist Party) of Kenya, which according to its manifesto aims ""to promote and protect individual rights and freedoms set forth in the Kenyan Constitution and to limit the scope of national government authority and spending.""<ref>[http://www.placentapartyofkenya.net/ ""Placenta Party of Kenya""] {{Webarchive
column3: date=24 December 2013 }} Retrieved on 20 October 2013.</ref><ref>Mango, Carole. [http://www.the-star.co.ke/news/article-85514/hellon-arunga-tell-coast-youth-reject-draft ""Hellon Arunga tell Coast youth to reject draft""] {{webarchive

column1: Timberlake came into the public eye after announcing his political ambitions in 2010<ref>[http://kenyadecides.co.ke/mp/quincy-timberlake/ ""Kenya Decides, Quincy Timberlake""] {{webarchive
column3: date=24 December 2013 }} Retrieved on 6 October 2013.</ref> and declaring that he would run for the [[Langata Constituency]] before the promulgation of the constitution. He later announced that he would contest the 2017 presidential election.<ref>Arlington, Darling. [http://www.allvoices.com/contributed-news/15781677-placenta-party-of-kenya-to-contest-2017-presidential-elections ""PlaCenta Party of Kenya to contest 2017 Presidential elections""] {{Webarchive

column1: The PlaCenta Party of Kenya was founded by Hellon, Timberlake and Arunga while they were still members of Hellon's Finger of God church.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KSEHtaYPm98, ""The Finger of God Trio Plans""]. [[Citizen TV]], 18 March 2010, Retrieved on 18 October 2013.</ref> Hellon later broke ties with the couple, claiming they had attempted to defraud him.<ref name=""trouble"">Kerongo, Grace. [http://www.the-star.co.ke/news/article-75228/finger-god-trouble-paradise ""Finger of God: Trouble in Paradise""] {{webarchive
column3: date=8 August 2014 }}, ''The Star'', 14 January 2011.</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WavFK2acyDw ""Joseph Helon Explains what happened to Esther Arunga""], KTN Kenya, 3 June 2014</ref>

column1: According to the party website, Project Take Back Kenya is an effort to break the rotational pattern of parties replacing names but featuring the same politicians at every election. The party's stated objective is to ""thrash the elite stranglehold on liberty, uniting Kenya's culturally diverse patriots who embrace traditional family values and restoring freedom of worship and expression.""<ref>[http://www.placentapartyofkenya.net/ ""Message from the President""] {{Webarchive
column3: date=24 December 2013 }}, Platinum Centraliser and Unionist Party. Retrieved on 20 October 2013.</ref>

column1: In 2010, Timberlake announced his intention to run for Prime Minister in the 2012 elections. A new Constitution was passed in the same year, bringing major amendments to the governing structure of the country.<ref>[https://www.voanews.com/a/kenyas-new-constitution-signed-into-law--101632883/124592.html ""Landmark moment as new Kenyan Constitution takes effect""], [[Voice of America]]. 26 August 2010.</ref> Timberlake then shifted his goal to contesting for the presidency. A number of court charges followed, which would have hindered him from contesting according to the law. Timberlake abandoned his presidential ambition and contested the seat of Lang'ata, the former PM's constituency.<ref>Kenya Decides. [http://kenyadecides.co.ke/mp/quincy-timberlake/ ""Quincy Timberlake for Lang'ata Constituency MP 2013""] {{webarchive
column3: date=24 December 2013 }}, [[Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission

column1: In February 2010, Hellon, Timberlake and Arunga announced their entry into politics under the umbrella of the PlaCenta Party of Kenya, with Hellon contesting for the presidency and Arunga for the seat of [[Karachuonyo Constituency]] and as a contender for the seat of Deputy President.<ref>Kenya Decides 2013. Within hours of the announcement, Arunga and Hellon were arrested for being members of an illegal society, the Finger of God, an evangelical church which Mrs Timberlake had attended for a year. The church had been registered as legal by the government 5 years previously. Computers and laptops were destroyed, documents confiscated and vehicles impounded.<ref>[http://www.nation.co.ke/news/-/1056/866110/-/3ajj6xz/-/index.html ""Police arrest Arunga, Hellon""] ''The Daily Nation'', 21 February 2010</ref><ref>Momanyi, Bernard. column6: [https://web.archive.org/web/20141108045420/http://www.jambonewspot.com/how-raila-ordered-esther-arungas-forceful-abortion/ ""How Raila ordered Esther Arunga's forceful abortion""]}}, Jambo News Spot, 14 July 2012, Retrieved on 21 October 2013.</ref> Timberlake spent months behind bars but was finally released with no charges in May 2011. Arunga, who had previously broken off her engagement to another church member, married him on 3 March while he was still in custody.<ref name=weds>[http://www.capitalfm.co.ke/lifestyle/2010/03/04/esther-arunga-weds-quincy-timberlake/ ""Esther Arunga weds Quincy Timberlake""], Capital FM, 4 March 2010.</ref>

column66: Timberlake arriving from [[Nyayo House]] under tight security to face charges of being a member of a cult before Chief Magistrate Gilbert Mutembei]]\nIn February 2010, Hellon, Timberlake and Arunga announced their entry into politics under the umbrella of the PlaCenta Party of Kenya, with Hellon contesting for the presidency and Arunga for the seat of [[Karachuonyo Constituency]] and as a contender for the seat of Deputy President.<ref>Kenya Decides 2013. Retrieved on 16 October 2013.</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KSEHtaYPm98 ""The Finger of God Trio Plans""], Citizen TV, 18 March 2010, Retrieved on 18 October 2013.</ref> On the same day that they made the announcement, Arunga resigned from her job as a news anchor at [[Kenya Television Network]]. Within hours of the announcement, Arunga and Hellon were arrested for being members of an illegal society, the Finger of God, an evangelical church which Mrs Timberlake had attended for a year. The church had been registered as legal by the government 5 years previously. Computers and laptops were destroyed, documents confiscated and vehicles impounded.<ref>[http://www.nation.co.ke/news/-/1056/866110/-/3ajj6xz/-/index.html ""Police arrest Arunga, Hellon""] \'\'The Daily Nation\'\', 21 February 2010</ref><ref>Momanyi, Bernard. [http://www.capitalfm.co.ke/lifestyle/2010/02/22/esther-arunga-and-joseph-hellon-arrested/ ""Esther Arunga and Joseph Hellon arrested""]. [[98.4 Capital FM
column70: Capital FM]], 22 February 2010.</ref> Timberlake was also arrested; while the rest of the group was released on bail after 2 days, he and Arunga were held in police custody. They both claim to have been isolated and tortured.<ref>\'\'[[Kenyan Daily Post]]\'\', {{usurped
column71: [https://web.archive.org/web/20141108045420/http://www.jambonewspot.com/how-raila-ordered-esther-arungas-forceful-abortion/ ""How Raila ordered Esther Arunga\'s forceful abortion""]}}, Jambo News Spot, 14 July 2012, Retrieved on 21 October 2013.</ref> Timberlake spent months behind bars but was finally released with no charges in May 2011. Arunga, who had previously broken off her engagement to another church member, married him on 3 March while he was still in custody.<ref name=weds>[http://www.capitalfm.co.ke/lifestyle/2010/03/04/esther-arunga-weds-quincy-timberlake/ ""Esther Arunga weds Quincy Timberlake""], Capital FM, 4 March 2010.</ref>\n\nAfter being released from custody, Timberlake remained under house arrest for several months on suspicion of being in the country illegally<ref>Ombati, Cyrus. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?id=2000006846&cid=159&story=Timberlake%20held%20in%20probe%20into%20his%20nationality&articleID=2000006846, ""Timberlake held in probe into his nationality""], Nairobi, 2 April 2010, Retrieved on 16 October 2013.</ref> and planning a revolt against the government.<ref>Thuku, Wahome. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?id=%202000008648&cid=418&articleID=2000008648, ""Quincy Timberlake charged for passport forgery""], \'\'[[The Standard (Kenya)
column72: The Standard]]\'\', 28 April 2010.</ref><ref name=""Khalwale"">Ochami, David. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?id=%202000005386&cid=37&articleID=2000005386 ""Khalwale wants troublesome foreigners kicked out""], \'\'The Standard\'\', 11 March 2010.</ref> The arrests were widely publicised.<ref>Okungu, Jerry. [http://www.afroarticles.com/article-dashboard/Article/Esther-Arunga--TV-Personality-Dominates-Kenyan-Media-For-One-Whole-Week/201752, ""Esther Arunga; TV Personality Dominates Kenyan Media for One Whole Week""], AfroArticles, 24 February 2010, Retrieved on 16 October 2013.</ref>\n\nThe couple was presented before the court on charges including being members of an illegal society (the Finger of God) and illegally holding passports from various countries.<ref name=""standardmedia.co.ke"">Kwamboka, Evelyn, [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?articleID=2000005378&story_title=Arunga-charged-with-being-member-of-unlawful-sect, ""Arunga Charged With Being a Member of an Unlawful Sect.""], \'\'The Standard\'\', 11 March 2010.</ref> The cases were postponed for several months. At the trial Assistant Commissioner of Police Samuel Chumo testified that nothing unusual was found at Hellon\'s house.<ref>Daily Nation. [http://www.nation.co.ke/news/Nothing-unusual-at-Finger-of-God-house-/-/1056/929462/-/13wk25u/-/index.html ""Nothing \'Unusual\' at Finger of God House,""], \'\'[[The Daily Nation]]\'\' 31 May 2010.</ref> The court dismissed a total of 36 charges.<ref name=tells>Muchiri, John and Ngaira, Amos. [http://www.nation.co.ke/News/The%20%20Quincy%20saga%20rages%20on/-/1056/895852/-/5wfg9q/-/index.html ""Arunga\'s partner tells all""], \'\'[[The Daily Nation]]\'\', 9 April 2010.</ref><ref>Mukei, Catherine and Kerongo, Grace. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?articleID=2000060975, ""Esther Arunga: My life is in danger""], \'\'The Standard\'\', 3 July 2012.</ref><ref>Kerongo, Grace. [http://www.the-star.co.ke/news/article-11546/someone-help-esther-arungas-children ""Someone help Esther Arunga\'s Children!""] {{webarchive
column76: date=25 December 2013 }}, \'\'The Star\'\', 6 July 2012.</ref><ref>Muendo, Stevens. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?id=2000021208&cid=123&articleID=2000021208, ""This is my confession""], \'\'The Standard\'\', 29 October 2010.</ref><ref>Kwamboka, Evelyn. [http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/?id=2000004013&cid=4&articleID=2000004013 ""Hellon charged, Arunga takes tests""], \'\'The Standard\'\', 23 February 2010.</ref><ref>Ombati, Cyrus. column1: '''Samuel Chumel Moroto''' (born 1960) is a Kenyan politician. He represents [[Kapenguria Constituency]] in the Kenyan National Assembly of the Kenyan parliament. He belongs to the [[Kenya African National Union]] (KANU) party. He is a career teacher and trade unionist. He was first elected to parliament in 2002. He hails from the Pokot community which mainly inhabits [[West Pokot County]].

He is a teacher by profession. Between 1983 and 1988, he served as an untrained teacher. He was promoted to the level of deputy headteacher in 1989 and to that of headteacher in 1995. Moroto is currently an pursuing a Bachelor of Arts at [[Daystar University]].
In 1996, Moroto was elected to the position of [[Kenya National Union of Teachers]] (KNUT) chairman, West Pokot branch. He was elected again in 1999 for the position of branch executive secretary.

He was first elected as an MP in the 2001 Kapenguria by-election occasioned by the death of the then MP, Francis Polisi Lotodo. He was re-elected in the 2002 Kenyan general elections. In 2006, Moroto was appointed by president [[Mwai Kibaki]] to the position of assistant minister, Ministry of Public Health and Sanitation.
Moroto lost the 2007 elections to Reverend Murgor mainly due to an [[Orange Democratic Movement
column2: ODM]] wave that swept the [[Rift valley]] region. He however bounced back in the 4 March 2013, general elections by defeating his closest opponent by a margin of more than 500 votes.

column1: Murumbi was born as Joseph Murumbi-Zuzarte. He was the [[illegitimate]] son of a [[Goan]] trader, Peter Nicholas Zuzarte, by the daughter of a [[Maasai people
column2: Maasai]] medicine man. His parents broke up when he was a toddler. His father married a Goan widow named Ezalda Clara Albuquerque, who already had nine children. He was then sent away to [[India]] for his schooling at the age of six. He went to Good Shepherd Convent School and then [[St Joseph's Boys' High School, Bangalore
column3: St. Joseph's High School]], both in [[Bangalore]]. He completed his schooling at St. Pancras European Boys High School in [[Bellary]].<ref>{{cite news

column2: title=Piecing together the fascinating story of Goan migration

column1: After returning to Kenya from England, where he had worked as a translator for the Moroccan Embassy in London, Murumbi became a member of the [[Kenya African Union]] political party, amidst a political ferment in East Africa caused by the beginning of the withdrawal from the African continent of the [[British Empire]]. A declaration of the [[State of Emergency]] in Kenya on 20 October 1952 saw the detention of senior figures of the Kenya African Union's leadership, and Murumbi found himself thrust into the center of the party's leadership as its acting Secretary-General. He played a key role in securing legal counsel for the detainees arrested in the emergency crackdown, and, together with [[Pio Gama Pinto]], raised objections to the continuance of British Imperial dominion in Kenya through Indian newspapers such as the ''Chronicle''. In March 1953, however, Murumbi was forced to flee the country to avoid arrest by the British authorities. With the assistance of the Indian High Commissioner [[Apa Pant]], Murumbi flew to India on an agricultural scholarship and spent time in India, Egypt and the United Kingdom building political connections and raising awareness of the detentions of prominent Kenyans by British authorities. Murumbi spent much of this period working with sympathetic nationalists in the Indian Government, which allowed him to write extensively in the Indian press and broadcast on [[All India Radio]].<ref>{{Cite journal
column7: title=African Internationalisms and the Erstwhile Trajectories of Kenyan Community Development: Joseph Murumbi's 1950s

column1: After Kenya became independent of British imperial rule in 1963, Murumbi participated in the writing of its first governmental constitution, and held the office of its Minister of Foreign Affairs from 1964 to 1966, touring the globe to set up numerous ambassadorial offices in foreign capitals for the newly created nation. He subsequently served as the Republic's Vice President in a government led by [[Jomo Kenyatta]] in 1966 for nine months. However, around this time Murumbi became uneasy with what he perceived as Kenyatta's increasing authoritarianism in dealing with political opponents, and the increasing corruption that he witnessed rapidly developing within the new Kenyan government order, and subsequently his concerns were borne out when Kenyatta began to use government power to engage in [[land grabbing]] in the late 1960s and 1970s. Murumbi also became further alienated from the new Kenyan governing order when Pio Gama Pinto, a close personal friend and key political philosophical mentor of Murumbi's, was murdered in April 1965 after he had become a public critic of it. As Pheroze Nowrojee stated:

''The assassination of Pinto illustrated to Murumbi the shocking extent to which the new government had departed from its promises. His feeling, evidently, was that these were not the principles for which so many had suffered, and his departure (from the new political order in power) was only a matter of time.''
After resigning from the office of the Vice-President in November 1966 through which was officially announced at the time to be on account of ill health, Murumbi withdrew from politics.

After leaving politics Murumbi became the acting chairman of the Kenyan National Archives, and later co-founded 'African Heritage' with Alan Donovan, which went on to become the largest [[Pan-African]] art gallery on the continent.<ref>{{Cite news

In 1982 he seriously injured himself in a fall at his home, and was reliant upon a wheelchair in his final years. He died on 22 June 1990 in his 79th year. Murumbi's body was buried in [[Nairobi]] City Park. The unmarked grave was subject to neglect, vandalism and theft through the late 1990s and early 2000s, and had at one time been threatened with being lost altogether when a building development scheme was considered for the site of the grave, until it was protected by the creation around it of a memorial garden named after him.<ref>'Friends of City Park' website (2007). https://friendsofcitypark.org/things-to-do/joseph-murumbi-peace-memorial-garden/</ref>

Murumbi married Sheila, a librarian whom he met whilst he was a political exile from Kenya in England in the late 1950s. They lived in Kenya subsequently on an estate in the Muthaiga district. She died in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web
column3: title=Joe Murumbi Died of a Broken Heart - The East African

column1: He was an avid art collector, and during his life acquired over 50,000 books and sheaves of official correspondence. The [[Kenya National Archives]] established a library containing some of the 8000 rare books (published before 1900) entrusted to them upon the death of Murumbi. The [[Kenya National Archives]] also created the 'Murumbi Gallery' within the same building, displaying the different African artifacts that were collected by him through his life.<ref>{{cite news

Murumbi was born as Joseph Murumbi-Zuzarte. He was the [[illegitimate]] son of a [[Goan]] trader, Peter Nicholas Zuzarte, by the daughter of a [[Maasai people
column73: Maasai]] medicine man. His parents broke up when he was a toddler. His father married a Goan widow named Ezalda Clara Albuquerque, who already had nine children. He was then sent away to [[India]] for his schooling at the age of six. He went to Good Shepherd Convent School and then [[St Joseph's Boys' High School, Bangalore
column74: St. Joseph's High School]], both in [[Bangalore]]. He completed his schooling at St. Pancras European Boys High School in [[Bellary]].<ref>{{cite news\n
column77: title=Piecing together the fascinating story of Goan migration\n
column80:
work=[[Deccan Herald]]}}</ref>

""), Section(title='==Political career==', content=""
After returning to Kenya from England, where he had worked as a translator for the Moroccan Embassy in London, Murumbi became a member of the [[Kenya African Union]] political party, amidst a political ferment in East Africa caused by the beginning of the withdrawal from the African continent of the [[British Empire]]. A declaration of the [[State of Emergency]] in Kenya on 20 October 1952 saw the detention of senior figures of the Kenya African Union's leadership, and Murumbi found himself thrust into the center of the party's leadership as its acting Secretary-General. He played a key role in securing legal counsel for the detainees arrested in the emergency crackdown, and, together with [[Pio Gama Pinto]], raised objections to the continuance of British Imperial dominion in Kenya through Indian newspapers such as the ''Chronicle''. In March 1953, however, Murumbi was forced to flee the country to avoid arrest by the British authorities. With the assistance of the Indian High Commissioner [[Apa Pant]], Murumbi flew to India on an agricultural scholarship and spent time in India, Egypt and the United Kingdom building political connections and raising awareness of the detentions of prominent Kenyans by British authorities. Murumbi spent much of this period working with sympathetic nationalists in the Indian Government, which allowed him to write extensively in the Indian press and broadcast on [[All India Radio]].<ref>{{Cite journal
column86: title=African Internationalisms and the Erstwhile Trajectories of Kenyan Community Development: Joseph Murumbi's 1950s
column96:
hdl-access=free }}</ref>

""), Section(title='==Ministerial career==', content=""
After Kenya became independent of British imperial rule in 1963, Murumbi participated in the writing of its first governmental constitution, and held the office of its Minister of Foreign Affairs from 1964 to 1966, touring the globe to set up numerous ambassadorial offices in foreign capitals for the newly created nation. He subsequently served as the Republic's Vice President in a government led by [[Jomo Kenyatta]] in 1966 for nine months. However, around this time Murumbi became uneasy with what he perceived as Kenyatta's increasing authoritarianism in dealing with political opponents, and the increasing corruption that he witnessed rapidly developing within the new Kenyan government order, and subsequently his concerns were borne out when Kenyatta began to use government power to engage in [[land grabbing]] in the late 1960s and 1970s. Murumbi also became further alienated from the new Kenyan governing order when Pio Gama Pinto, a close personal friend and key political philosophical mentor of Murumbi's, was murdered in April 1965 after he had become a public critic of it. As Pheroze Nowrojee stated:

''The assassination of Pinto illustrated to Murumbi the shocking extent to which the new government had departed from its promises. His feeling, evidently, was that these were not the principles for which so many had suffered, and his departure (from the new political order in power) was only a matter of time.''

After resigning from the office of the Vice-President in November 1966 through which was officially announced at the time to be on account of ill health, Murumbi withdrew from politics.

In 1982 he seriously injured himself in a fall at his home, and was reliant upon a wheelchair in his final years. He died on 22 June 1990 in his 79th year. Murumbi's body was buried in [[Nairobi]] City Park. The unmarked grave was subject to neglect, vandalism and theft through the late 1990s and early 2000s, and had at one time been threatened with being lost altogether when a building development scheme was considered for the site of the grave, until it was protected by the creation around it of a memorial garden named after him.<ref>'Friends of City Park' website (2007). https://friendsofcitypark.org/things-to-do/joseph-murumbi-peace-memorial-garden/</ref>
